questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial review in operation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：党派性杰利蝾螈（partisan gerrymandering）是否属于联邦法院不能审的政治问题（political question），所以这案子能不能直接进实体审理。

三秒认题路径：

划分选区 → 党派操控 → 政治问题 → 无司法标准 → 不能审实体

核心法律规则

政治问题原则（political-question doctrine）的考场意思：有些争议不是法院来判输赢，而是宪法交给其他政治部门，或者法院根本没有可操作的标准来判。

这里最关键的是：党派性杰利蝾螈（partisan gerrymandering）在 Rucho v. Common Cause 里被认定为不可司法解决的问题，所以联邦法院不能就其实体作出裁判。

换句话说，题目不是在问“这张地图坏不坏”，而是在问“法院能不能依法给出可执行的判标准”，答案是不能。

核心判例：Rucho v. Common Cause — 党派性选区划分没有可供法院操作的标准，所以通常属于非可审理的政治问题。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决吗？
NO 这里不是终局上诉题，而是司法审查（judicial review）能不能介入实体争议。
再问：宪法把这类问题留给法院了吗？
NO 党派性杰利蝾螈（partisan gerrymandering）属于政治问题（political question）。
第三步：法院有没有可操作标准？
KILL 没有 judicially discoverable and manageable standards，所以不能判实体。
结论：联邦法院不应审理实体，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州议会故意偏袒本党、结果票数和席位明显失衡，法院当然应该出手。

但考试真正问的是：法院有没有可司法管理的标准来判这个问题，而不是这张地图看起来公不公平。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「政治上看起来多不公平」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干明确写了州议会按党派目的重画选区，这正是 partisan gerrymandering；Rucho 说这类争议没有法院可操作标准，所以不能审实体。

❌ 概念混淆 | 主体免诉误判

✕ B: 把 Eleventh Amendment 误当成拦住州官员禁令诉讼的理由。

❌ 法律适用 | 保证共和制误判

✕ C: 把 Guarantee Clause 当成法院可直接裁判的依据。

❌ 事实误判 | 等人口已满足

✕ D: 题干已说各选区人口相等，one person, one vote 不是问题点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是政治问题，再查有没有司法标准；只要标准缺席，法院就停在门口。

考场速记

记住一句：政治问题不是“政治味很重”，而是“法院没法按法律标准判”。

看到党派性选区划分，先联想 Rucho v. Common Cause；看到“可立即上诉”那套口诀时，再想 In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely（injunction、certification、class action 等例外）。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city ordinance requires that its mayor must have been continuously a resident of the city for at least five years at the time he or she takes office. The plaintiff, who is thinking about running for mayor in an election that will take place next year, will have been a resident of the city for only four and one-half years at the time the elected mayor would take office. Before he decides to run for mayor, the plaintiff wants to know whether he could lawfully assume that position if he were elected.
As a result, the plaintiff files suit in the local federal district court for a declaratory judgment that the city's five-year-residence requirement is unconstitutional and that he is entitled to a place on his political party's primary election ballot for mayor. He names the chairman of his political party as the sole defendant and does not join any election officials. The chairman responds by joining the plaintiff in requesting the court to declare the city's residence requirement invalid.
What should the court do in this case?

choices.A: Issue the declaratory judgment, because a residency requirement of this type is a denial of the equal protection of the laws.
choices.B: Issue the declaratory judgment, because the plaintiff will have substantially complied with the residency requirement.
choices.C: Refuse to determine the merits of this suit, because there is no case or controversy.
choices.D: Refuse to issue the declaratory judgment, because an issue of this kind involving only a local election does not present a substantial federal constitutional question.

questions.explanation:
Article III of the Constitution limits federal judicial power to actual cases or controversies—ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. This case-or-controversy requirement is not met unless the plaintiff has standing—ie, a personal stake in the outcome of the case. To have standing, the plaintiff must allege three elements:

  • Injury-in-fact – actual or imminent harm that is concrete and particularized
  • Causation – the injury is fairly traceable to the defendant's challenged conduct
  • Redressability – a favorable judicial decision will likely remedy or prevent the alleged injury

Here, the plaintiff sued to have the city's residency requirement invalidated. But he has not suffered actual or imminent harm since he has merely thought about running for mayor and any injury to him is purely hypothetical (no injury-in-fact). And even if the plaintiff could allege such harm, he still lacks standing because that injury would not be fairly traceable to the chairman of his political party (no causation). Therefore, there is no actual case or controversy, and the court should refuse to determine the merits of this suit.

(Choice A) The residency requirement triggers the equal protection clause since it discriminates against persons who have lived in the city for less than five years. But this does not create an actual case or controversy since the plaintiff still lacks standing.

(Choice B) The fact that the plaintiff will have "substantially complied" with the residency requirement if and when he runs for mayor is no basis for the court to declare the requirement invalid.

(Choice D) The plaintiff's suit does present a substantial federal constitutional question since it challenges the constitutionality of the city's residency requirement. As a result, the court has subject-matter jurisdiction to hear this suit. But it cannot adjudicate the suit because there is no case or controversy.

📌 Educational Objective

Article III's case-or-controversy requirement is not met unless the plaintiff has standing—ie, suffered an injury-in-fact that was caused by the defendant's challenged conduct and is redressable by the courts.

📚 References
  • Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560–61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).
questions.zh-question:
某市法令规定，市长在就职时必须已在该市连续居住至少五年。原告正考虑参加明年举行的市长选举，但在当选市长就职之时，其在该市的居住时间仅为四年半。在决定参选之前，原告想知道如果他当选，是否能够合法地担任该职位。

因此，原告向当地联邦地区法院提起诉讼，请求宣告式判决，认定该市的五年居住要求违宪，并且他有权被列入其政党的市长初选选票上。他将自己政党的主席列为唯一被告，并未将任何选举官员列为共同被告。该主席作出回应，与原告一同请求法院宣布该市的居住要求无效。

在这种情况下，法院应如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 作出宣告式判决，因为此类居住要求剥夺了法律的平等保护。
zh-choices.B: 作出宣告式判决，因为原告将已实质性地满足了居住要求。
zh-choices.C: 拒绝就本案的实体问题作出裁决，因为不存在“案件或争议”。
zh-choices.D: 拒绝作出宣告式判决，因为此类仅涉及地方选举的问题，并未构成重大的联邦宪法问题。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial review in operation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原告还没真的受到、也没有马上会受到具体伤害时，联邦法院能不能先替他做宪法判断。

三秒认题路径：

没受伤 → 只是打算参选 → 诉求只是假设 → standing 不足 → 不能审实体

核心法律规则

联邦法院只能审 实际案件或争议（case or controversy），所以原告必须先有 诉讼资格（standing）。伤害事实（injury-in-fact） 要求的是已经发生，或马上会发生的、具体而个人化的伤害；只是“以后可能想参选”还不够。

因果关系（causation） 要求伤害能追到被告的行为；可救济性（redressability） 要求法院判赢后真的能改善你的处境。这里原告还没遭遇现实伤害，而且被告还是政党主席，不是直接实施住宅年限要求的选举官员，所以这案子先卡在 standing。

核心判例：Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife 说明 standing 必须同时有伤害事实、因果关系和可救济性，少一个就不能进实体。

思维导图

1. 伤害事实
只是“打算以后参选”，还没被市政规则现实挡住。
2. 因果关系
被告是党主席，不是直接做出选举资格限制的官员。
3. 可救济性
就算法院宣告无效，也不能修补一个尚未发生的假想伤害。
卡死结论
三项要件缺前两项，直接停在 没有 case or controversy。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：五年居住要求看起来像是歧视，应该直接判违宪。

但考试真正问的是：原告现在有没有足够具体的伤害，足以让联邦法院先开门审案。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「这个规定看起来公不公平」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里原告只是“想参选”，还没有现实、具体、可归责的伤害，standing 不够，所以法院不能先审实体。

❌ 概念混淆 | 平等保护套错

✕ A: 把违宪争议直接当成可起诉，忽略了先要有 standing。

❌ 事实误判 | 预期受损夸大

✕ B: “substantially complied” 不是这里的门票，原告连现实损害都还没发生。

❌ 法律适用 | 司法管辖误判

✕ D: 题目有联邦问题不等于能直接判实体，jurisdiction 和 standing 是两关。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看 case or controversy，再拆 standing 三要件；没伤害就别急着讨论违宪。

考场速记

记住一句：先问“有没有真正受伤”，再问“能不能救济”。只要还是假设性的未来计划，联邦法院通常不会开门。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify missing constitutional standing elements

reason.en: A merely contemplated candidacy makes the alleged injury hypothetical rather than actual or imminent.
reason.zh: 仅考虑参选使所称损害属于假设，而非现实或即将发生。

reason.en: Declaratory relief still requires an actual Article III case or controversy.
reason.zh: 宣告性救济仍须存在宪法第三条所要求的实际案件或争议。

reason.en: The identity of the sole defendant exposes the absence of causation and effective redressability.
reason.zh: 唯一被告的身份揭示了因果关系及有效救济可能性的缺失。

keywords.text: does not join any election officials

reason.en: No official capable of enforcing or altering ballot eligibility is before the court.
reason.zh: 法院面前没有能够执行或改变选票资格的官员。

reason.en: The chairman's agreement with the plaintiff underscores the absence of a genuine adversarial dispute.
reason.zh: 党主席赞同原告进一步表明不存在真正的对立争议。

A.text: denial of the equal protection of the laws

reason.en: This addresses the constitutional merits but ignores the threshold absence of standing.
reason.zh: 该表述涉及宪法实体问题，却忽略了原告缺乏诉讼资格这一门槛问题。

reason.en: Near compliance neither satisfies the ordinance nor establishes Article III standing.
reason.zh: 接近满足条件既不等于符合条例，也不能确立宪法第三条诉讼资格。

reason.en: A federal court cannot reach the merits when Article III standing is absent.
reason.zh: 缺乏宪法第三条诉讼资格时，联邦法院不得审理实体问题。

label.zh: 宪法第三条案件或争议缺失

reason.en: This correctly identifies the constitutional consequence of the missing standing elements.
reason.zh: 该表述正确指出缺少诉讼资格要件所产生的宪法后果。

label.zh: 地方选举管辖权干扰项

reason.en: A local setting does not eliminate a substantial federal question arising from a constitutional challenge.
reason.zh: 地方选举背景不会消除宪法挑战所产生的重大联邦问题。

reason.en: The suit presents a federal constitutional question, but subject-matter jurisdiction does not cure the standing defect.
reason.zh: 本案提出联邦宪法问题，但事项管辖权不能弥补诉讼资格缺陷。

highlights.text: who is thinking about running for mayor

reason.en: The plaintiff has not committed to running, so his alleged injury is neither actual nor imminent.
reason.zh: 原告尚未决定参选，因此其所称损害既非现实也非即将发生。

highlights.text: Before he decides to run for mayor

reason.en: This timing confirms that the dispute rests on a contingent future decision.
reason.zh: 这一时点表明争议取决于未来尚未作出的决定。

highlights.text: does not join any election officials

reason.en: The alleged ballot injury is not traceable to the named chairman, and relief against him would not control election officials.
reason.zh: 所称选票损害无法追溯至被列名的党主席，对其作出的救济也不能约束选举官员。

highlights.text: The chairman responds by joining the plaintiff in requesting the court to declare the city's residence requirement invalid.

reason.en: The parties seek the same result, reinforcing that no concrete dispute with the enforcing authority exists.
reason.zh: 双方寻求同一结果，进一步表明其与执行机关之间不存在具体争议。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Assume that Congress passed and the President signed the following statute: "The appellate jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court shall not extend to any case involving the constitutionality of any state statute limiting the circumstances in which a person may obtain contraception, or involving the constitutionality of this statute."
What is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of this statute?

choices.A: Congress may not exercise its authority over the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in a way that seriously interferes with the establishment of a supreme and uniform body of federal constitutional law.
choices.B: Congress may only regulate the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over cases initially arising in federal courts.
choices.C: The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court may only be altered by constitutional amendment.
choices.D: The statute violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

questions.explanation:
Jurisdiction of United States Supreme Court

Most cases come before the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) through its appellate jurisdiction. This allows SCOTUS to review certain cases that have been decided by a lower federal court or a state's highest court. Article III grants Congress the power to regulate and make exceptions to SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. But when exercising this almost unlimited power, Congress cannot violate:

  • the separation-of-powers doctrine—eg, usurping judicial power to decide cases—or
  • other constitutional provisions—eg, giving only men the right to appeal, in violation of the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment.

Here, the federal statute denies SCOTUS appellate jurisdiction over any case involving the constitutionality of a state statute limiting access to contraception. As a result, the federal statute may violate the separation-of-powers doctrine since it could usurp SCOTUS's power to establish a supreme and uniform body of federal constitutional law on this issue. Therefore, this is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of the federal statute.

(Choices B & C) Since Article III of the Constitution gives Congress the power to limit SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction over cases initially arising in federal or state court, no constitutional amendment is required.

(Choice D) The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause applies when states treat similarly situated persons differently. But since the challenged statute was enacted by the federal government, this clause does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Article III grants Congress the power to regulate and limit SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. But when exercising this power, Congress cannot violate the separation-of-powers doctrine or other constitutional provisions.

📚 References
  • United States v. Klein, 80 U.S. 128, 147–48 (1871) (establishing that Congress cannot alter the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction if it would violate the separation-of-powers doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
假设国会通过并由总统签署了以下法令：“美国最高法院的上诉管辖权不应延伸至任何涉及州法规合宪性的案件，该州法规限制了女性可获得堕胎的情形，也不应延伸至涉及本法令合宪性的案件。”

反对该法令合宪性的最有力论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 国会行使其对最高法院上诉管辖权的权力时，不得严重干涉建立一个最高且统一的联邦宪法法律体系。
zh-choices.B: 国会仅能规范最高法院对最初在联邦法院提起的案件的上诉管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 最高法院的上诉管辖权只能通过宪法修正案来变更。
zh-choices.D: 该法令违反了《第十四修正案》的平等保护条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能否限制最高法院的上诉管辖权，但不能用这个权限去掐掉宪法审查，破坏联邦宪法统一解释。

三秒认题路径：

国会限管辖 → 最高法院上诉权 → 宪法审查案 → 统一联邦法 → 违宪风险

核心法律规则

《宪法》第三条让国会可以调整最高法院的上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction），考场意思：不是所有案件都必须让 SCOTUS 直接复审。

但国会不能借这个权力去干预司法机关的核心功能，尤其不能让最高法院无法建立统一的联邦宪法解释；这会碰到分权（separation of powers）红线。

所以，上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction）可以被“收窄”，但不能被收窄到让某类宪法争议永远躲开最高法院的最终统一控制。

核心判例： United States v. Klein - 国会不能通过管辖限制，实质上剥夺最高法院完成统一宪法解释的功能。

思维导图

先问：国会是在调 最高法院上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction） 吗？
是第三条通常允许国会做“exceptions and regulations”。
再问这个限制是不是在卡掉整类宪法争议的最终统一解释？
卡死点：如果它让最高法院不能建立“supreme and uniform” 的联邦宪法法，就踩到分权红线。
本题事实只排除“涉及限制避孕获取的州法合宪性”的案件，以及“涉及该联邦法本身合宪性”的案件。
结论这不是普通的程序调门，而是在针对特定宪法争议抽掉最高法院终局复核，最强反对理由就是 分权受损。
答案落点：选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：国会既然能“exceptions” 最高法院的上诉管辖权，那它把某类案件排除出去也没问题。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有把这个权力用到会破坏最高法院统一解释宪法的程度，而不是单纯看它有没有写进法条。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干直接把 涉及某类州法合宪性 的案件整体排除在最高法院上诉管辖之外，这最强的问题就是会不会妨碍统一联邦宪法解释。

❌ 概念混淆 | 初审来源误判

✕ B: 误把“上诉管辖权”当成只能管 federal courts 的初审案。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对修宪误判

✕ C: 把国会限管辖误听成必须修宪才行。

❌ 事实误判 | 联邦主体偷换

✕ D: 题目是联邦国会立法，不是州政府差别对待。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看国会有没有在碰第三条，再判断限制是不是会掏空最高法院的统一宪法解释功能。

考场速记

记住一句：国会能调最高法院上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction），但不能调到让联邦宪法法失去统一出口。

遇到“管辖限制”题，先想 United States v. Klein：能限，不是无限；一旦动到分权和统一解释，就要警惕违宪。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify separation-of-powers limits on jurisdiction stripping

reason.en: Identifies Congress as the government actor restricting jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 表明限制管辖权的政府行为主体是国会。

reason.en: Article III permits congressional exceptions to this jurisdiction, subject to constitutional limits.
reason.zh: 第三条允许国会对此管辖权规定例外，但仍受宪法限制。

reason.en: Its role in maintaining uniform federal constitutional law supports the separation-of-powers objection.
reason.zh: 其统一联邦宪法法律的职能构成分权异议的依据。

keywords.text: shall not extend to any case

reason.en: The sweeping exclusion threatens the Court's ability to ensure uniform constitutional interpretation.
reason.zh: 这种全面排除可能妨碍最高法院统一解释宪法。

reason.en: Removing review of state constitutional questions risks divergent federal constitutional rules.
reason.zh: 排除对州法宪法问题的审查可能导致联邦宪法规则不统一。

keywords.text: limiting the circumstances in which a person may obtain contraception

reason.en: Defines the specific constitutional subject insulated from Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 界定了被排除在最高法院审查之外的特定宪法议题。

label.zh: 自我屏蔽的管辖权条款

reason.en: The statute also attempts to prevent Supreme Court review of its own validity.
reason.zh: 该法还试图阻止最高法院审查其自身效力。

reason.en: Identifies the degree of interference supporting a separation-of-powers challenge.
reason.zh: 表明足以支持分权原则挑战的干预程度。

A.text: a supreme and uniform body of federal constitutional law

reason.en: Preserving uniform constitutional law is the central basis for the strongest objection.
reason.zh: 维护宪法法律的统一性是最有力异议的核心依据。

reason.en: Incorrectly narrows Congress's Article III authority.
reason.zh: 错误缩小了国会依据第三条享有的权限。

B.text: cases initially arising in federal courts

reason.en: Congress may regulate appellate jurisdiction over cases originating in either federal or state court.
reason.zh: 国会可规制源于联邦法院或州法院案件的上诉管辖权。

C.text: only be altered by constitutional amendment

reason.en: Incorrectly denies Congress's express Article III exceptions power.
reason.zh: 错误否定了第三条明确赋予国会的例外规定权。

D.text: equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment

label.zh: 针对州行为的平等保护条款

reason.en: This clause restricts state action, while the challenged statute is federal.
reason.zh: 该条款约束州行为，而受质疑的法律属于联邦立法。

highlights.text: The appellate jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court shall not extend to any case

label.zh: 全面剥夺最高法院上诉管辖权

reason.en: This sweeping removal of appellate review creates the separation-of-powers concern.
reason.zh: 这种全面取消上诉审查的做法引发分权原则问题。

highlights.text: constitutionality of any state statute

reason.en: Excluding these cases may prevent uniform resolution of federal constitutional questions.
reason.zh: 排除此类案件可能妨碍联邦宪法问题的统一解决。

highlights.text: or involving the constitutionality of this statute

reason.en: The statute attempts to insulate its own constitutionality from Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 该法试图使其自身合宪性免受最高法院审查。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A drawbridge owned, operated, and maintained by a county government malfunctioned. A portion of the drawbridge fell and collided with a boat owned by a man who resides in another state. The man filed a lawsuit against the county in a federal district court to recover for the damage caused to his boat. The county has moved to dismiss the suit.
Is the court likely to grant the county's motion?

choices.A: No.
choices.B: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against county governments in federal court.
choices.C: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment gives state courts exclusive jurisdiction over suits against state, county, and municipal governments.
choices.D: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has original and exclusive jurisdiction over suits against governments.

questions.explanation:
Eleventh Amendment
(state immunity from suit in federal court)
Immunity
  • Suit brought by private party or foreign government
  • Suit against state official violating state law
  • Exceptions:
    • State consents to suit
    • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
    • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief for alleged constitutional violation
    • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
    • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
No
immunity
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
  • Eminent domain proceedings
  • Suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war & armed forces

The Eleventh Amendment prohibits foreign governments and private parties from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. However, this immunity does not extend to actions brought against local governments (e.g., municipalities, counties) (Choice B). Therefore, the Eleventh Amendment does not apply to the man's suit against the county, and the federal court will likely deny the county's motion to dismiss.

(Choice C) The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states all powers that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government. However, it does not give state courts exclusive jurisdiction over suits against state, county, and municipal governments. Instead, state and federal courts have concurrent jurisdiction over such suits.

(Choice D) The U.S. Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over cases that affect ambassadors, public ministers, or consuls OR that involve a state as a party (neither seen here). Additionally, the Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over suits between states (also not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Eleventh Amendment bars suits against state governments in federal court. However, this immunity does not extend to suits against local governments (e.g., counties, municipalities).

📚 References
  • N. Ins. Co. v. Chatham County, 547 U.S. 189, 193–95 (2006) (holding that the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit suits against local governments).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 918 (2020) (explaining that the Eleventh Amendment does not bar suits against local governments in federal court).
questions.zh-question:
一个由县政府拥有、运营和维护的吊桥发生故障。吊桥的一部分坠落，并与一名居住在另一州的男子的船只相撞。该男子在联邦地区法院对该县提起诉讼，以索赔其船只所遭受的损害。该县已提出驳回此项诉讼的动议。

法院是否可能批准该县的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会。
zh-choices.B: 会，因为《Eleventh Amendment》禁止在联邦法院对县政府提起诉讼。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为《Tenth Amendment》赋予州法院对州、县和市政府提起的诉讼拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为美国最高法院对针对政府的诉讼拥有初审和专属管辖权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第十一修正案（Eleventh Amendment）只挡州，不挡县；县政府被告在联邦法院里通常不能靠它撤诉。

三秒认题路径：

县政府被告 → 联邦法院 → 第十一修正案 → 先看“州” → 不是州就不挡

核心法律规则

第十一修正案（Eleventh Amendment）的考场意思：它主要保护的是州政府（state）不被私人在联邦法院告；县（county）、市（municipality）这类地方政府通常不享有这层免诉保护。

所以这题先别被“政府被告”吓到，要看被告是不是州本身。题干告的是县政府，规则直接落到“no immunity”。

核心判例：N. Ins. Co. v. Chatham County — 直接说明第十一修正案不禁止针对地方政府的联邦诉讼。

思维导图

先问：被告是不是“州”本身？
YES私人告州 → 先想 Eleventh Amendment。
再看是否有例外：州同意、国会有效废除、官员前瞻性救济等。
本题没有这些例外。
NO被告是县/市/地方政府 → 不走州主权免诉。
题干是county government，所以直接跳出第十一修正案挡箭牌。
结论：联邦法院不会因第十一修正案而驳回。
答案落点：A. No

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目里有“政府”，所以Eleventh Amendment一定能用。

但考试真正问的是：这个被告是不是州政府（state government），不是泛泛地看“是不是政府部门”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

县政府不是州，命题人就是想骗你把“州免诉”错误扩成“所有政府免诉”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的county government只是地方政府，不是州；第十一修正案不挡这种被告，所以联邦法院不该因免诉驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州县混同

✕ B: 把Eleventh Amendment硬套到县政府身上了。

❌ 法律适用 | 十修误搬

✕ C: 把Tenth Amendment当成管诉讼管辖的条文了。

❌ 事实误判 | 司法权偷换

✕ D: 把最高法院的原始管辖权偷换成普通县侵权案了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清被告层级：先看是不是州，再决定要不要启动第十一修正案。

考场速记

记住一句：Eleventh Amendment挡的是州，不挡县和市；看到地方政府被告，先别自动点“免诉”。

本题速记：state yes, county no。若题目真在考中间上诉，再想口诀“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A jury convicted a federal district court judge of bribery. When the judge subsequently refused to resign from his office, the House of Representatives adopted and presented to the Senate an article of impeachment that charged the judge with bribery. Pursuant to its rules for impeachment, the Senate authorized a committee of senators to hold closed-door hearings to take testimony and receive evidence related to the impeachment charge. At the conclusion of the hearings, the committee reported the facts and summarized the evidence to the full Senate. Based on the committee's report, the Senate voted to convict the judge and remove him from office.
The judge has filed suit in federal court to enjoin the Senate from removing him from office. The judge claims that the Senate violated Article I of the U.S. Constitution by prohibiting the full Senate from taking part in the hearings.
If the court dismisses the judge's action, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.A: The action involves a nonjusticiable political question.
choices.B: The action is moot.
choices.C: The judge lacks standing.
choices.D: The U.S. Supreme Court has original and exclusive jurisdiction over the action.

questions.explanation:
Nonjusticiable political questions
(issues incapable of judicial resolution)
  • Recognition of foreign governments
  • Reception of ambassadors
  • Nature of wars/hostilities
  • Partisan gerrymandering
  • Guarantee of republican form of government
  • Recognition of Native American tribes
  • House/Senate rules for impeachment
  • Ratification process for constitutional amendments

Article III of the U.S. Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide justiciable cases and controversies. However, some actions are not capable of judicial resolution (ie, nonjusticiable). This includes actions implicating the political-question doctrine. Under this doctrine, federal courts are prohibited from deciding political questions that should be resolved by another branch of government. A case presents a nonjusticiable political question when:

  • the issue has been reserved to the executive or legislative branch and/or
  • there is a lack of judicially discoverable and manageable standards to resolve the issue.

Here, the judge seeks to enjoin the Senate from removing him from office. He claims that the Senate violated Article I of the U.S. Constitution by prohibiting the full Senate from participating in the evidentiary hearings. However, the impeachment and removal of federal judges is a power reserved solely to Congress,* and there are no standards to help a court resolve an impeachment process issue. Therefore, the court will most likely dismiss the judge's action because it involves a nonjusticiable political question.

*Congress also has the exclusive power to impeach and remove the President, Vice President, and other federal officers (eg, the U.S. Attorney General).

(Choice B) A suit is also nonjusticiable if it is moot—ie, when the suit no longer presents an actual controversy for the court to resolve. Here, the judge's action is not moot since his harm has not been resolved. However, the federal courts cannot provide relief because his claim presents a nonjusticiable political question.

(Choice C) The judge has standing because he suffered an injury-in-fact (removal from office) that was caused by the challenged action (impeachment procedure) and is redressable by the remedy sought (injunction).

(Choice D) The U.S. Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over cases that affect ambassadors, public ministers, or consuls OR involve a state as a party (neither seen here). Additionally, the Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over suits between states (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Federal courts must dismiss a suit that presents a nonjusticiable political question. This occurs when (1) the Constitution reserves the issue to another branch of government and/or (2) the court lacks judicially discoverable and manageable standards to resolve the issue.

📚 References
  • Nixon v. United States, 506 U.S. 224, 238 (1993) (holding that the impeachment process presents a nonjusticiable question that is reserved to the legislative branch).
  • Baker v. Carr, 369 U.S. 186, 210–17 (1962) (explaining the political-question doctrine).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Fed. Courts § 574 (2020) (listing common examples of political questions).

一个陪审团裁定一名联邦地区法院法官犯有贿赂罪。当该法官随后拒绝辞去其职务时，众议院通过并向参议院提交了一项弹劾条款，指控该法官犯有贿赂罪。根据其弹劾规则，参议院授权一个参议员委员会举行闭门听证会，就弹劾指控听取证词和接收证据。听证会结束后，该委员会向参议院全体会议报告了事实并总结了证据。根据该委员会的报告，参议院投票裁定该法官有罪并将其免职。

该法官已向联邦法院提起诉讼，请求禁止参议院将其免职。该法官声称，参议院禁止参议院全体会议参加听证会，违反了 U.S. Constitution (美国宪法) 第一条。

如果法院驳回该法官的诉讼，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该诉讼涉及一个不可由司法审理的政治问题。
zh-choices.B: 该诉讼已无实际意义。
zh-choices.C: 该法官缺乏诉讼资格。
zh-choices.D: U.S. Supreme Court (美国最高法院) 对此诉讼拥有初审和专属管辖权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial review in operation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：法官想用联邦法院去拦住国会弹劾和罢免程序，这类问题通常属于 政治问题原则（political-question doctrine），法院不进场。

三秒认题路径：

弹劾程序 → 国会权限 → 无司法标准 → 不可裁判 → 选 A

核心法律规则

联邦法院只能裁判 justiciable case or controversy（可裁判争议）；如果争议被宪法交给另一分支处理，或法院没有可操作的判断标准，就会触发 political-question doctrine（政治问题原则），法院直接驳回。

本题里，impeachment（弹劾） 和罢免程序是国会专属权力，法官要法院去审“参议院内部听证规则对不对”，法院没有一套能接手的标准，所以不能立刻发禁令。

这不等于案子没伤害，而是“这件事不是法院该管的题目”。所以考场上先问：是不是国会自己保留的程序？如果是，通常就卡在政治问题原则。

核心判例： Nixon v. United States — 弹劾程序属于参议院处理的政治问题，法院不审参议院内部怎么做。

思维导图

先问：这是 final judgment（终局判决） 吗？
否。 这是要法院马上发禁令，去干预参议院的弹劾处理。
再问：有没有国会明确允许的中间上诉？
没有。 题干没给 statutory interlocutory appeal（法定中间上诉）。
最后问：能不能走 collateral-order doctrine（附带命令原则）？
要同时满足重要性、独立性、以及 effectively unreviewable。
卡死点：即使现在不让上诉，终局后仍可做法律救济；但本题更早就死在“政治问题原则”这一关。
结论：法院看到的是“国会弹劾程序”
直接联想 Nixon：参议院内部弹劾流程，不是法院该替你重做的题。
答案： A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：法官被“罢免”了，听起来很像自己的权利被侵害，法院应该帮他审。
但考试真正问的是：这是不是法院能判的题，而不是这件事严不严重。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的骗点是把“程序不公平”包装成“可以司法审查”。但只要问题本身是国会弹劾规则，命题人就是在逼你认出 nonjusticiable political question（不可裁判的政治问题）。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干在问国会弹劾程序和参议院内部规则，属于 impeachment 这种政治问题，法院没有标准可管，所以应驳回。

❌ 事实误判 | 把损害当终结

✕ B: 以为官职没了就自动 moot，但争议还在，只是法院不碰。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把资格当门槛

✕ C: 看到受损就想否定 standing，其实伤害、因果、救济都够。

❌ 法律适用 | 错搬专属管辖

✕ D: 把 original jurisdiction 乱套上去，但这案子不属于最高法院专属原审。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看争议是不是宪法交给国会的程序，再决定法院要不要进场。

考场速记

记住一句：弹劾、承认外国政府、宣战、党派性杰利蝾螈 这类题，先想政治问题原则，不要先冲 standing 或 moot。

口诀可记：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，但本题不是中间上诉例外，而是国会弹劾程序本身不可裁判。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state legislature recently enacted a statute forbidding public utilities regulated by the State Public Service Commission from increasing their rates more than once every two years.
A public utility company regulated by that commission has just obtained approval from the commission for a general rate increase. The company has routinely filed for a rate increase every 10 to 14 months during the last 20 years. Because of uncertainties about future fuel prices, the company cannot ascertain with any certainty the date when it will need a further rate increase, but it thinks that it may need such an increase sometime within the next 18 months.
The company files an action in the federal district court in the state requesting a declaratory judgment that this new state statute forbidding public utility rate increases more than once every two years is unconstitutional. Assume no federal statute is relevant.
How should the court rule in this case?

choices.A: Dismiss the complaint, because controversies over state-regulated utility rates are outside of the jurisdiction conferred on federal courts by Article III of the Constitution.
choices.B: Dismiss the complaint, because this action is not ripe for decision.
choices.C: Hold the statute constitutional, because the judgment of a legislature on a matter involving economic regulation is entitled to great deference.
choices.D: Hold the statute unconstitutional, because such a moratorium on rate increases deprives utilities of their property without due process of law.

questions.explanation:
Article III, Section 2 of the Constitution allows federal courts to hear cases and controversies that are ripe for adjudication (ie, capable of judicial resolution). This requirement is met when the plaintiff has suffered an actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. But a suit cannot be heard by a federal court if the plaintiff faces the mere possibility of harm (unripe) or the plaintiff's harm is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot).

Here, the company filed a complaint in federal court requesting a declaratory judgment regarding the new statute limiting rate increases for public utilities to once every two years. But since the company had just obtained approval for a rate increase and merely thinks that it may need another rate increase in the next 18 months, it has suffered no actual harm or immediate threat of harm. Therefore, this action is unripe and should be dismissed.

(Choice A) Article III grants federal courts subject-matter jurisdiction over claims arising under the Constitution, federal laws, or treaties. Therefore, the company's complaint regarding the constitutionality of the new statute falls within the court's conferred jurisdiction and will not be dismissed on this basis.

(Choices C & D) A determination as to whether (1) the court should defer to the legislature's economic judgment or (2) the moratorium is a deprivation of property without due process of law involves the merits of the suit. But since the action is not ripe for adjudication, the court cannot consider the merits and must dismiss the suit.

📌 Educational Objective

Federal courts can only hear cases and controversies that are ripe for adjudication—ie, claims that concern an actual or immediate threat of harm suffered by the plaintiff. Therefore, courts must dismiss claims that allege the mere possibility of harm (unripe) or harm that is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot).

📚 References
  • Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).
questions.zh-question:
某州立法机构最近颁布了一项法规，禁止受州公共服务委员会（State Public Service Commission）监管的公用事业公司每两年内涨价超过一次。

一家受该委员会监管的公用事业公司刚刚获得委员会批准，进行了一次全面的费率上调。在过去的20年里，该公司通常每10到14个月申请一次费率上调。由于未来燃料价格的不确定性，该公司无法确定何时需要再次提高费率，但它认为在未来18个月内的某个时间可能需要再次涨价。

该公司向该州的联邦地区法院提起诉讼，请求作出宣告性判决，认定这项禁止公用事业公司每两年涨价超过一次的新州法规违宪。假设没有相关的联邦法规。

法院应如何裁决此案？

zh-choices.A: 驳回诉状，因为关于州监管的公用事业费率的争议，不在《宪法》第三条（Article III of the Constitution）授予联邦法院的管辖权范围之内。
zh-choices.B: 驳回诉状，因为此诉讼的审理时机尚未成熟。
zh-choices.C: 裁定该法规合宪，因为立法机构在涉及经济监管事项上的判断应得到高度尊重。
zh-choices.D: 裁定该法规违宪，因为这种暂停费率上调的做法未经正当法律程序即剥夺了公用事业公司的财产。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial review in operation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦法院能不能立刻审理一项还没真正伤到原告的州法挑战，也就是 成熟性（ripeness）；现在只是“可能以后会需要涨价”，所以还不能进实体审查。

三秒认题路径：

还没损害 → 只会可能受伤 → ripeness 不够 → 先别谈合宪 → 直接驳回

核心法律规则

案件成熟性（ripeness） 的考试意思：法院只管已经发生、或已经逼近到不能再等的伤害；如果只是“也许将来会出事”，就先不审。实际损害（actual harm） 或 立即威胁（immediate threat） 才够，单纯可能性不够。

这题里，公司刚拿到这次涨价批准，只是说自己也许在未来 18 个月内还会再申请，所以现在没有真实伤害，也没有马上要来的伤害。mere possibility of harm 还不够立案，法院应当先以不成熟为由驳回。

核心判例： Texas v. United States —— 说明只有现实或迫近的伤害才成熟，单纯猜测未来会受影响不够。

思维导图

先问：这案子已经能给法院“现在就判”吗？
YES： 已经有真实伤害 / 迫近威胁 → 可以进入实体审查。
NO： 只有未来可能再涨价，还是猜测。
再卡一层： 只是“可能以后需要再申请”，不是马上会被新法卡住。
卡死点：ripeness 不足，连合宪性都先不谈。
结论： 先驳回，答案是 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然新法限制两年一次涨价，企业以后真涨不了价，当然很“伤”。

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题不是在比谁更委屈，而是在问现在有没有可审的现实争议；这里只有未来猜测，所以还不成熟。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是：公司刚拿到批准，只说未来 may need such an increase，没有当前损害，所以 ripeness 不够，法院应驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 司法管辖误判

✕ A: 把 subject-matter 当成门槛，但这里不是没管辖权，而是还没成熟。

❌ 法律适用 | 经济审查误套

✕ C: 看到经济监管就想用“高度尊重”，但法院连实体都不该先碰。

❌ 事实误判 | 财产权受损偷换

✕ D: 把未来可能涨价说成 due process 侵害，但题干还没出现现实剥夺。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先看有没有现实争议，再决定能不能进实体合宪性审查。

考场速记

记住一句：先看有没有现在的伤，再谈以后会不会伤。 这题的口诀就是“ripeness 不够，先别审实体”。

如果以后考到可立即上诉的例外，顺手联想：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定中间上诉例外。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A baseball fan has a fierce temper and an extremely loud voice. Attending a baseball game in which a number of calls went against the home team, the fan repeatedly stood up, brandished his fist, and angrily shouted, "Kill the umpires." The fourth time he engaged in this conduct, many other spectators followed the fan in rising from their seats, brandishing fists, and shouting, "Kill the umpires."
The home team lost the game. Although no violence ensued, spectators crowded menacingly around the umpires after the game. As a result, the umpires were able to leave the field and stadium only with the help of a massive police escort.
For his conduct, the fan was charged with inciting to riot and was convicted in a jury trial in state court. He appealed. The state supreme court reversed his conviction. In its opinion, the court discussed in detail decisions of the United States Supreme Court dealing with the First Amendment free speech clause as incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment. At the end of that discussion, however, the court stated that it "need not resolve how, on the basis of these cases," the United States Supreme Court would decide the fan's case. "Instead," the court stated, "this court has always given the free-speech guarantee of the state's constitution the broadest possible interpretation. As a result, we hold that in this case, where no riot or other violence actually occurred, the state constitution does not permit this conviction for incitement to riot to stand."
The United States Supreme Court grants a writ of certiorari to review this decision of the state supreme court.
In this case, how should the United States Supreme Court rule?

choices.A: Affirm the state supreme court's decision, because the fan's ballpark shout is commonplace hyperbole that cannot, consistent with the First and Fourteenth Amendments, be punished.
choices.B: Dismiss the writ as improvidently granted, because the state supreme court's decision rests on an independent and adequate state-law ground.
choices.C: Remand the case to the state supreme court with directions that it resolve the First and Fourteenth Amendment free-speech issue that it discussed in such detail.
choices.D: Reverse the decision of the state supreme court, because incitement to violent action is not speech protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

questions.explanation:
The Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) may use its discretionary appellate jurisdiction and grant a writ of certiorari to review state court judgments. But since SCOTUS may only review such judgments if they are based on federal law, it cannot review a judgment based on adequate and independent state grounds. This occurs when:

  • state law fully resolves the matter, so the outcome of the case is not affected by federal law (adequate) and
  • the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its decision (independent).

If a writ of certiorari was improvidently (ie, incorrectly) granted in such a case, SCOTUS must dismiss the writ.

Here, the state supreme court reversed the fan's criminal conviction for inciting a riot on a state constitutional ground. The court held that the state constitution grants broader free-speech protection than the U.S. Constitution (adequate ground). And though the court discussed First Amendment cases in detail, it clearly stated that its decision was not based on that caselaw (independent ground). Therefore, the state supreme court's decision rests on an independent and adequate state ground, and SCOTUS must dismiss the writ as improvidently granted.

(Choices A & D) When a case is decided on adequate and independent state grounds (as seen here), SCOTUS has no jurisdiction to affirm or reverse that case on its merits. As a result, SCOTUS cannot decide whether the fan's ballpark shout is commonplace hyperbole or unprotected speech subject to punishment.

(Choice C) The state court need not resolve the federal constitutional issue since its decision was based on an adequate and independent state ground. But even if the decision was not based on such a ground, SCOTUS would not ask the state court to resolve the federal constitutional issue. Instead, it would rule on that issue and remand the case to state court to resolve any remaining state-law issues.

📌 Educational Objective

SCOTUS only has jurisdiction to review a state supreme court decision based on federal law—not adequate and independent state grounds.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1040–41 (1983) (explaining when a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state grounds).
questions.zh-question:
一名棒球迷脾气暴躁，嗓门极大。在一场棒球比赛中，由于数次判罚对主队不利，该球迷屡次站起，挥舞拳头，并愤怒地高喊：“杀了裁判！”当他第四次做出此行为时，许多其他观众也跟着他从座位上站起来，挥舞拳头，并高喊：“杀了裁判！”

主队输掉了比赛。虽然没有发生暴力事件，但赛后观众们气势汹汹地围住裁判。结果，裁判们只有在大批警察的护送下才能离开球场和体育馆。

因其行为，该球迷被指控煽动骚乱，并在州法院经陪审团审判后被定罪。他提起了上诉。州最高法院推翻了他的定罪。在其判决意见中，该法院详细讨论了美国最高法院关于First Amendment言论自由条款（该条款已并入Fourteenth Amendment）的判例。然而，在该讨论的结尾，该法院声明，“无需基于这些案例来解决”美国最高法院将如何裁决该球迷的案件。该法院声明：“相反，本法院一向对州宪法中的言论自由保障给予最宽泛的解释。因此，我们裁定，在本案中，鉴于并未实际发生骚乱或其他暴力事件，州宪法不允许维持这项煽动骚乱的定罪。”

美国最高法院签发了调卷令（writ of certiorari），以复审州最高法院的此项判决。

在本案中，美国最高法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 维持州最高法院的判决，因为该球迷在球场上的呼喊是常见的夸张言辞，根据First Amendment和Fourteenth Amendment，不应受到惩罚。
zh-choices.B: 以调卷令签发不当为由予以驳回，因为州最高法院的判决基于独立且充分的州法律依据。
zh-choices.C: 将案件发回州最高法院重审，并指示其解决其曾详细讨论过的First Amendment和Fourteenth Amendment的言论自由问题。
zh-choices.D: 推翻州最高法院的判决，因为煽动暴力行为不属于受First Amendment和Fourteenth Amendment保护的言论。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州最高法院虽然谈了联邦宪法问题，但真正判决依据是独立且充分的州法理由时，联邦最高法院是否要撤回受理并不进入实体审查。

三秒认题路径：

州判决 → 先看依据 → 独立州法 → 充分州法 → 撤回受理

核心法律规则

这条规则怎么用

联邦最高法院（Supreme Court of the United States）可以用 certiorari（调卷令） 审查州法院判决，但前提是该判决必须建立在联邦法问题上。若州法院的裁判有 adequate and independent state ground（充分且独立的州法理由），联邦最高法院就没有权力改判实体，只能 dismiss the writ as improvidently granted（撤销错误受理）。这里的“考场意思”很直接：州法院已经用州宪法把案子定死了，联邦法讨论再多也不改变结果。Michigan v. Long 就是在告诉你，看到“州法足够解决 + 法院明确说不是靠联邦法”，就要想到不能进入实体审查。

核心判例： Michigan v. Long — 州法院裁判如果立足于充分且独立的州法理由，SCOTUS 只能撤回受理，不能按联邦宪法实体去改判。

思维导图

州最高法院判决，SCOTUS 能直接判实体吗？
先问1：这是 final judgment（终局判决） 吗？
这里不是在拼证据对错，而是在看 联邦法院有没有管辖权。
先问2：有没有 adequate and independent state ground（充分且独立的州法理由）？
充分：州法足以单独决定输赢。
独立：州法院明确说，结论不是靠联邦宪法判出来的。
卡死点：州法院已明确说“不是基于联邦法” + 州宪法给了更宽保护 → 联邦法讨论再细，也不能改结果。
结论：B. 撤回受理

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州最高法院既然详细讨论了 First Amendment（第一修正案），SCOTUS 就应该去改它的联邦法判断。

但考试真正问的是：州法院最后到底靠什么理由赢下案件，不是它中间讨论了多少联邦法案例。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题里州法院最后说的是：州宪法给更宽言论保护，所以本案不能定罪；这就是独立且充分的州法理由，SCOTUS 不能顺手改成“其实联邦法也允许处罚”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 州最高法院明确以州宪法更宽保护作结论，且说不是基于联邦法，所以属于充分且独立的州法理由，SCOTUS 只能撤回受理。

❌ 概念混淆 | 实体审查误判

✕ A: 把“激烈喊叫”直接当成可罚言论，忽略了本题先卡管辖权。

❌ 法律适用 | 发回补判误判

✕ C: 想让州法院再答联邦题，但 SCOTUS 先要看是否已有独立州法终局。

❌ 事实误判 | 讳言州法结论

✕ D: 盯着“Kill the umpires”就冲实体，漏掉州法院已用州宪法把案子解决。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看管辖权，再看州法理由是否独立且充分；只要这一步成立，就别被联邦宪法讨论带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：州法院判决如果有 adequate and independent state ground（充分且独立的州法理由），SCOTUS 不能改实体，只能 dismiss the writ as improvidently granted。

这类题先找“州法是否已经单独定输赢”，再想联邦法；联邦法说得再多，也可能只是背景，不是可审查 आधार。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law that restricted access to contraception was challenged in state court as a violation of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution and as a violation of a similar due process provision of the state constitution. The case made its way to the state's highest court, which ruled that the law violated the due process provisions of both the U.S. and the state constitutions.
If petitioned to do so, may the U.S. Supreme Court exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision?

choices.A: No, because the state court's decision in this case rests on adequate and independent state law grounds.
choices.B: No, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction only over state court decisions that determine the constitutionality of federal laws.
choices.C: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over any ruling of a state's highest court based on an interpretation of federal law.
choices.D: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over decisions that find state laws in violation of the federal Constitution.

questions.explanation:
Appellate jurisdiction of SCOTUS
Type of review Applicability
Certiorari
(discretionary review)
  • Appeal from lower federal court or highest state court by filing petition for writ of certiorari
  • SCOTUS will review if ≥ 4 Justices vote to accept appeal
  • Very common – how most cases come before SCOTUS
Direct appeal
(mandatory review)
  • Appeal from decision on injunction by special three-judge federal district court panel
  • Extremely rare – limited to cases brought under specific statutes (eg, Voting Rights Act)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has discretionary jurisdiction to review final state court decisions that involve federal law. But SCOTUS cannot exercise jurisdiction to review those decisions if they rest on adequate and independent state grounds—ie, when:

  • state law completely resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case (adequate) and
  • the state court did not rely on federal law to decide the state law issue (independent).

This limit on SCOTUS's jurisdiction promotes judicial economy by barring SCOTUS from deciding a federal question when it would not change the outcome of the case.

Here, the highest state court's ruling rests on an adequate state ground because the court found the law invalid under the state constitution. So even if SCOTUS reversed the state court's ruling on the U.S. Constitution, the law would still violate the state constitution and the outcome of the case would remain the same. The ruling also rests on an independent state ground because the state court did not rely on federal law in ruling on the similar state constitutional issue.* As a result, SCOTUS may not exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision.

*A state court ruling is not independent if the state court relied on an "identical" federal provision to rule on the state provision. Here, the federal and state due process provisions are similar but not the same, so the ruling rests on an independent state ground.

(Choice B) SCOTUS has appellate jurisdiction over state court decisions determining the constitutionality of federal laws AND the validity of state laws under the U.S. Constitution.

(Choices C & D) SCOTUS has appellate jurisdiction over state court decisions based on federal law—including decisions that find state laws in violation of the federal constitution—unless that decision rests on adequate and independent state grounds.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court has no jurisdiction to review state court decisions based on adequate and independent state grounds—ie, when state grounds completely resolve the matter and the court does not rely on federal law to reach that decision.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (explaining when a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state grounds).

一项限制获取避孕措施的州法律在州法院受到挑战，理由是其违反了美国宪法第十四修正案的“正当程序条款”（due process clause），以及州宪法中类似的正当程序条款。该案件最终上诉至该州的最高法院，该法院裁定该法律违反了美国宪法和州宪法的正当程序条款。
如果收到申请，美国最高法院是否可以行使管辖权审查该州法院的裁决？

zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为美国最高法院仅对裁定联邦法律合宪性的州法院裁决拥有上诉管辖权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州最高法院虽然也写了联邦宪法理由，但如果州宪法理由已经足够独立地支持结果，美国最高法院（Supreme Court of the United States, SCOTUS）就不能管。

三秒认题路径：

州最高法院 → 也判州法错 → 看州理由独立吗 → 看州理由够吗 → 不能复审

核心法律规则

最终州法院判决（final state court decision）如果同时涉及联邦法，SCOTUS通常可以受理；但前提是这个判决不是建立在充分且独立的州法依据（adequate and independent state grounds）上，考场意思：州法自己已经把案子“判死”了，联邦问题就算翻转也改变不了结果。

adequate的考场意思：州法理由单独就够把结果撑住。independent的考场意思：州法院没有拿联邦法来解释州法条文，州理由不是“借联邦法的力”。

所以，如果州最高法院已经说“这部法同时违反州宪法”，而这个州宪法理由足以维持裁判，SCOTUS就算同意联邦宪法部分，也救不回这部州法。

核心判例： Michigan v. Long — 它告诉你：只要州判决落在充分且独立的州法基础上，SCOTUS就不进场。

思维导图

州最高法院判了“州法 + 联邦法”都违宪，SCOTUS 能不能审？
第1问：这是最终州法院判决吗？
如果不是最终判决，先别谈 SCOTUS。
第2问：有没有联邦法问题？
有，但这题还要继续看州法理由会不会独立地把结果撑住。
第3问：州法理由是否 adequate？
州宪法自己就能让该法无效，说明联邦法改判也不改结果。
第4问：州法理由是否 independent？
州法院没依赖联邦法来解释州宪法，所以独立成立。
结论：州法 grounds 已经够独立 → 答案 A：不能受理

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然州最高法院已经认定联邦宪法也被违反，SCOTUS 应该能直接复审。

但考试真正问的是：州法理由是不是已经单独把案子做完了；如果州宪法足够支撑结果，联邦问题只是“多写了一层”，并不打开 SCOTUS 大门。

司法考试看的是「州程序/州法上能不能独立定案」，而不是「联邦宪法有没有被顺手提到」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 state constitution 已经足以维持结果，所以即使联邦宪法部分被改判，结论也不会变，SCOTUS 不能审。

❌ 概念混淆 | 联邦法范围误判

✕ B: 把 SCOTUS 权限缩成只管 federal laws，漏掉它也管州判决里的联邦问题。

❌ 法律适用 | 独立依据漏看

✕ C: 只盯着“有联邦法”就冲，忘了先排除州法已经独立定案。

❌ 事实误判 | 结果可改写错看

✕ D: 看到联邦宪法违宪就以为一定能上诉，忽略 state grounds 已把结果锁死。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看最终性，再查州法是否充分且独立；只要州理由足够，联邦问题就不再决定结果。

考场速记

记住一句话：州理由先把案子做死，SCOTUS 就不进场。 看到州最高法院同时写州宪法和联邦宪法时，先问“州法是不是已经够独立、够充分”。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 用来记中间上诉例外；但这题不是例外题，核心还是 adequate and independent state grounds。

question_analysis.skill_tested: identify limits on Supreme Court review

reason.en: The challenged law may be reviewed under both federal and state constitutional provisions.
reason.zh: 该法律可能同时受到联邦和州宪法条款的审查。

keywords.text: due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment

label.zh: 第十四修正案正当程序保障

reason.en: This federal constitutional claim would ordinarily support Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 该联邦宪法主张通常可构成最高法院审查的依据。

keywords.text: similar due process provision of the state constitution

label.zh: 独立的州宪法正当程序条款

reason.en: It supplies a potentially independent state ground that separately invalidates the law.
reason.zh: 该条款可能构成独立的州法依据，单独使该法律无效。

reason.en: Supreme Court review of a state judgment generally requires a final decision from the highest available state court.
reason.zh: 最高法院审查州法院判决通常要求该判决来自可受理案件的州最高法院。

keywords.text: both the U.S. and the state constitutions

label.zh: 联邦与州宪法双重依据

reason.en: The state constitutional holding preserves the result regardless of any federal-law reversal.
reason.zh: 即使联邦法判决被推翻，州宪法判决仍会维持原结果。

reason.en: This identifies the precise issue as the Court's jurisdiction over the state judgment.
reason.zh: 这明确指出争点是最高法院对该州法院判决是否具有管辖权。

A.text: adequate and independent state law grounds

label.en: adequate and independent state grounds doctrine
label.zh: 充分且独立的州法依据原则

reason.en: This doctrine bars Supreme Court review because resolving the federal issue cannot change the judgment.
reason.zh: 由于解决联邦问题无法改变判决结果，该原则排除最高法院审查。

label.zh: 过度狭窄的管辖权限制

reason.en: Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction is not limited to this category of state court decisions.
reason.zh: 最高法院的上诉管辖权并不限于此类州法院判决。

reason.en: The Court may also review whether state laws violate the federal Constitution.
reason.zh: 最高法院也可审查州法律是否违反联邦宪法。

label.zh: 过度宽泛的上诉管辖权主张

reason.en: The word ignores the exception for adequate and independent state grounds.
reason.zh: 该措辞忽略了充分且独立的州法依据这一例外。

C.text: based on an interpretation of federal law

reason.en: A federal question generally permits review but does not overcome an independently dispositive state ground.
reason.zh: 联邦问题通常允许审查，但不能克服具有独立决定作用的州法依据。

D.text: state laws in violation of the federal Constitution

label.zh: 依据联邦宪法宣告州法无效

reason.en: Such decisions are generally reviewable, but not when an adequate and independent state holding controls the outcome.
reason.zh: 此类判决通常可受审查，但当充分且独立的州法判决控制结果时除外。

label.zh: 绝对化的上诉管辖权主张

reason.en: The statement omits the jurisdictional exception created by dispositive state grounds.
reason.zh: 该陈述遗漏了决定性州法依据所形成的管辖权例外。

highlights.text: due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution

reason.en: This creates the federal issue that would ordinarily permit Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 这形成了通常允许最高法院审查的联邦问题。

highlights.text: a similar due process provision of the state constitution

reason.en: This signals a state-law basis capable of independently sustaining the judgment.
reason.zh: 这表明存在可独立维持判决的州法依据。

highlights.text: the law violated the due process provisions of both the U.S. and the state constitutions

reason.en: The state constitutional holding means reversal of the federal holding would not alter the outcome.
reason.zh: 州宪法判决意味着即使推翻联邦法判决也不会改变结果。

highlights.text: may the U.S. Supreme Court exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision

label.zh: 对州法院判决的审查管辖权

reason.en: The issue is jurisdiction, not whether the constitutional ruling was substantively correct.
reason.zh: 争点是管辖权，而不是宪法判决在实体上是否正确。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress passed a statute providing that parties could no longer seek review in the U.S. Supreme Court of final judgments in criminal matters made by the highest court in each state.
What is the best argument supporting the constitutionality of the statute?

choices.A: Congress has the power to make exceptions to the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
choices.B: Criminal matters are traditionally governed by state law.
choices.C: The proper means of federal judicial review of state criminal matters is by habeas corpus.
choices.D: The review of state court judgments is not within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.explanation:
SCOTUS jurisdiction
Type Definition Applicability
Original
(Congress cannot adjust) 		Case filed directly in SCOTUS Cases involving either:
• ambassador/public minister/consul or
• state as party
Appellate
(Congress may limit) 		Case filed after decision by either:
• lower federal court or
• highest state court
All other cases by either:
• writ of certiorari or
• direct appeal (rare)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has appellate jurisdiction to review a final judgment of lower federal courts and the highest state courts when the judgment turns on federal law. But the Article III exceptions clause gives Congress almost unlimited power to regulate or make exceptions to this jurisdiction. Therefore, that is the best argument supporting the constitutionality of the statute prohibiting SCOTUS from reviewing final judgments in criminal matters made by the highest court in each state.

(Choice B) Although criminal matters are traditionally governed by state law, SCOTUS can review final judgments in state criminal cases involving an alleged violation of the Constitution, a federal law, or a treaty.

(Choice C) A person in custody can file a petition for a writ of habeas corpus in federal court to challenge the legality of his/her detention. But a habeas corpus petition is a separate civil suit—not part of the criminal appeals process. So, the better argument is that Congress can make exceptions to SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction.

(Choice D) The review of state court judgments is not within SCOTUS's very limited original jurisdiction (ie, power to hear a case first and render a decision). But it is within SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction extends to final judgments of lower federal courts and the highest state courts when the judgment turns on federal law. But the Article III exceptions clause gives Congress extensive power to regulate and make exceptions to this jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • Ex parte McCardle, 74 U.S. 506, 514 (1869) (establishing that Congress has almost unlimited power to make exceptions to the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
国会通过了一项法规，规定当事人不得就各州最高法院对刑事案件作出的终审判决，再向美国最高法院 (U.S. Supreme Court) 寻求复审。

支持该法规合宪性的最佳论据是什么？

zh-choices.A: 国会有权对最高法院 (Supreme Court) 的上诉管辖权制定例外。
zh-choices.B: 刑事案件传统上由州法律管辖。
zh-choices.C: 对州刑事案件进行联邦司法复审的适当方式是通过人身保护令 (habeas corpus)。
zh-choices.D: 对州法院判决的复审不属于最高法院 (Supreme Court) 的初始管辖权范围。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能否用 例外条款（Exceptions Clause） 限制最高法院的 上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction），所以这条法案能不能站住脚。

三秒认题路径：

最高法院 → 最终判决 → 国会限权 → 例外条款 → 选 A

核心法律规则

美国最高法院（Supreme Court）对州最高法院和下级联邦法院的终局判决，通常行使 上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction）。但宪法第三条的 例外条款（Exceptions Clause） 让国会可以对这项管辖权作出限制，甚至排除某些类别的复审。

考场意思：这题不是问“案子重不重要”，而是问“国会能不能把这类案子从最高法院的上诉入口里拿掉”。答案是能，所以法案通常合宪。

核心判例： Ex parte McCardle — 它直接说明国会几乎可以对最高法院的上诉管辖权作出例外。

思维导图

先看：这是最高法院的 原始管辖权（original jurisdiction） 吗？
否。 州最高法院作出的终局判决，走的是 上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction）。
再看：国会有没有权限把这一类案件排除出去？
有。 Exceptions Clause 允许国会对最高法院上诉管辖权作例外和限制。
卡死点：不是“州刑事案能不能审”，而是“国会能不能砍掉最高法院的上诉入口”
结论：该 statute 合宪，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：刑事案件一直主要由州法管，或者可以改走 habeas corpus（人身保护令），所以国会不该挡住复审。

但考试真正问的是：国会能不能调整最高法院的 上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction），不是州法传统分工，也不是别的救济渠道够不够用。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干直接在砍 最高法院对州最高法院终局判决的复审入口，而 Exceptions Clause 允许国会这样做，所以法案合宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州法传统误判

✕ B: 把 traditionally 当成禁令，忽略联邦宪法问题照样能上最高法院。

❌ 法律适用 | 救济路径误判

✕ C: 把 habeas corpus 当成替代上诉审查的唯一通道。

❌ 事实误判 | 原始管辖偷换

✕ D: 盯着 original jurisdiction 说事，题干问的却是上诉管辖权能否被限制。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清原始管辖和上诉管辖，再用例外条款直接判断国会能否限权。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，先记住联邦程序里的法定中间上诉例外，再回头看国会是否已把入口关掉。

question_analysis.skill_tested: identify congressional control over appellate jurisdiction

reason.en: Identifies Congress as the actor regulating Supreme Court jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 表明由国会对最高法院管辖权进行规制。

reason.en: Signals that appellate rather than original jurisdiction is involved.
reason.zh: 表明涉及的是上诉管辖权而非初审管辖权。

label.en: Supreme Court of the United States

reason.en: Identifies the federal court whose jurisdiction Congress has restricted.
reason.zh: 确定国会所限制管辖权的联邦法院。

reason.en: Final judgments are the decisions ordinarily eligible for Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 终局判决通常属于最高法院可审查的裁判。

reason.en: Defines the category of cases removed from Supreme Court review.
reason.zh: 界定被排除在最高法院审查之外的案件类别。

reason.en: Review of this court's judgments falls within Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 对该法院判决的审查属于最高法院的上诉管辖权。

reason.en: States Congress's Article III power to restrict Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 表明国会依据宪法第三条限制最高法院上诉管辖权的权力。

reason.en: Correctly classifies review of final state-court judgments.
reason.zh: 正确界定了对州法院终局判决进行审查的管辖权类型。

reason.en: State control of criminal law does not eliminate Supreme Court review of federal issues.
reason.zh: 刑法通常由州法调整，并不排除最高法院审查其中的联邦问题。

reason.en: Habeas corpus is a separate civil proceeding, not the exclusive appellate route.
reason.zh: 人身保护令是独立的民事程序，并非唯一的刑事上诉途径。

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests that habeas corpus is the required method of federal review.
reason.zh: 错误暗示人身保护令是联邦审查的必经方式。

reason.en: Invokes the wrong jurisdictional category because review is appellate.
reason.zh: 审查州法院判决属于上诉管辖，因此该选项混淆了管辖权类别。

reason.en: This review is outside original jurisdiction but within appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 该审查不属于初审管辖权，但属于上诉管辖权。

highlights.text: Congress passed a statute

reason.en: Triggers the Article III Exceptions Clause analysis.
reason.zh: 触发对宪法第三条例外条款的分析。

highlights.text: could no longer seek review in the U.S. Supreme Court

reason.en: Frames whether Congress may remove a category from Supreme Court appellate review.
reason.zh: 提出国会能否将某类案件排除在最高法院上诉审查之外的问题。

highlights.text: final judgments in criminal matters

reason.en: Defines the judgments covered by the statutory jurisdictional restriction.
reason.zh: 界定该法定管辖权限制所涵盖的判决。

highlights.text: highest court in each state

reason.en: Confirms that any Supreme Court review would exercise appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 确认最高法院对此类判决的审查属于上诉管辖权。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In response to the need for additional toxic waste landfills in a state, the state's legislature enacted a law authorizing a state agency to establish five new state-owned and state-operated toxic waste landfills. The law provided that the agency would decide the locations and sizes of the landfills after an investigation of all potential sites and a determination that the particular sites chosen would not endanger public health and would be consistent with the public welfare.
A community in the state was scheduled for inspection by the agency as a potential toxic waste landfill site. Because the community's residents obtained most of their drinking water from an aquifer that ran under the entire community, a citizens' group, made up of residents of that community, sued the appropriate officials of the agency in federal court. The group sought a declaratory judgment that selecting their community as the site of a toxic waste landfill would be unconstitutional and an injunction preventing the agency from doing so. The agency officials moved to dismiss.
Which of the following is the most appropriate basis for the court to dismiss this suit?

choices.A: The case is not ripe for a decision on the merits.
choices.B: The case presents a nonjusticiable political question.
choices.C: The Eleventh Amendment bars suits of this kind in the federal courts.
choices.D: The interest of the state in obtaining suitable sites for toxic waste landfills is sufficiently compelling to justify the selection of the community as a location for such a facility.

questions.explanation:
Justiciability
(suitability for judicial resolution)
Case or controversy Prohibits advisory opinions under three doctrines:
  • Standing – plaintiff must allege injury-in-fact caused by challenged action & redressable by remedy sought
  • Ripeness – claim must present actual controversy involving past injury or present threat of injury
  • Mootness – claim must be unresolved
Adequate & independent state grounds SCOTUS cannot review final state court judgment that rests on adequate & independent state grounds
Political question Court cannot hear case if issue presented:
  • is reserved for executive/legislative branches or
  • lacks judicially manageable standards for resolution
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

A suit may only be heard by a federal court if it is justiciable. A suit is justiciable if it presents an actual case or controversy that is ripe for (and capable of) judicial resolution—ie, when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an imminent threat of harm. Therefore, a suit based on potential harm (unripe) or harm that is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot) should be dismissed.

Here, the group sued to prevent agency officials from selecting its community as a toxic waste landfill site. But the suit is based on potential—not actual or imminent—harm since the agency is still investigating where to place these landfills. Therefore, the most appropriate basis to dismiss this suit is that it is not ripe for a decision on the merits. But the group's claim may become justiciable and can be re-filed in federal court if its community is later selected as a landfill site.

(Choice B) The political-question doctrine prohibits federal courts from hearing cases that present issues that (1) are reserved for the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution. But since federal courts often determine the constitutionality of state laws, this doctrine is not a basis for dismissal.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court for monetary relief. But it does not bar suits against state officials for declaratory or injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice D) Federal courts can only determine the merits of a suit—eg, whether a government action is necessary to serve a compelling government interest (strict scrutiny)—if that suit is justiciable. And since this suit is not ripe for judicial resolution, the court cannot determine the merits of the group's claim.

📌 Educational Objective

To be justiciable, a suit must present an actual case or controversy. This occurs when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an imminent threat thereof—not a mere possibility of harm.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).
  • Abbot Labs. v. Gardner, 387 U.S. 136, 148 (1967) (stating that federal courts cannot adjudicate unripe suits).
questions.zh-question:
为响应州内对新增有毒废物填埋场的需要，该州立法机构颁布了一项法律，授权一个州级机构建立五个新的、州有并州营的有毒废物填埋场。该法律规定，在对所有潜在地点进行调查，并确定所选的特定地点不会危及公共健康且符合公共福利之后，该机构将决定填埋场的地点和规模。

该州的一个社区被该机构列为潜在的有毒废物填埋场选址，并计划进行考察。由于该社区的居民大部分饮用水来自流经整个社区地下的蓄水层，一个由该社区居民组成的公民团体在联邦法院起诉了该机构的相应官员。该团体寻求一项宣告性判决，认定选择他们的社区作为有毒废物填埋场是违宪的，并申请禁止该机构此行为的禁令。该机构官员提出驳回诉讼的动议。

以下哪一项是法院驳回此诉讼最适当的依据？

zh-choices.A: 本案据以作出实质性判决的时机尚未成熟。
zh-choices.B: 本案提出了一个不可由法院审理的政治问题。
zh-choices.C: 《第十一修正案》禁止在联邦法院进行此类诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 该州在获取有毒废物填埋场合适选址方面的利益，具有足够的强制性，足以证明选择该社区作为此类设施的地点是正当的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：成熟性（ripeness），也就是现在能不能进法院；题干只有“可能被选址”的风险，还没到能判的阶段。

三秒认题路径：

还在调查 → 只是潜在伤害 → 没有现实争议 → 不成熟 → 不能现在审

核心法律规则

可司法裁判性（justiciability）要求先有真正的案件或争议（case or controversy）。成熟性（ripeness）考场意思：原告得拿出已经发生的损害，或者马上就要发生的威胁，不能只是“以后可能会被伤害”。

如果政府还在调查、还没决定选哪块地，原告只是担心自己社区“可能”会被选中，这就太早了。等社区真的被选定，或者伤害逼近到可预见时，再起诉才行。

核心判例：Abbott Labs. v. Gardner —— 联邦法院不能审理还没成熟的诉讼；先有现实或迫近伤害，才轮到法院。

思维导图

先问：现在有真正的争议吗？
YES已经有现实损害，或马上会发生的威胁 → 才能继续看实体。
NO这里只有“可能被选成垃圾填埋场”的担心，政府还在调查。
卡死点：只是潜在伤害，不是现在可裁判的争议 → ripeness 未成。
再看：有没有别的即时上诉入口？
没有这不是终局后复审的问题，而是先天就太早。
结论法院先 dismiss，等社区真的被选址后再来。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：社区喝水来自含水层，听起来伤害很严重，所以法院应该马上帮他们挡掉。

但考试真正问的是：现在有没有可裁判的现实争议。这里只是“将来可能被选址”，还不是已经发生或迫在眉睫的损害，所以先不审。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。本题的关键不是灾害多吓人，而是时机太早。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干只说社区scheduled for inspection，政府还在选址调查；这只是潜在伤害，所以案件还不成熟，不能现在判。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权力误读

✕ B: 把政府选址争议硬扯成政治问题，但法院本来就能审州法合宪性。

❌ 事实误判 | 主体偷换

✕ C: 这里告的是州官员要禁令，不是州本身索赔，Eleventh Amendment 挡不住。

❌ 法律适用 | 审查层级错位

✕ D: 把“是否有正当公共利益”当成先决问题，但没成熟时根本还轮不到实体审查。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先看有没有现实争议，再谈能不能进入实体审查。

考场速记

记住一句：ripeness 看的是“现在能不能告”，不是“未来会不会受伤”。如果只有可能性，没有现实或迫近伤害，就先 dismiss。

可顺带记口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，但那是中间上诉例外；本题不是上诉问题，而是成熟性不过关。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute admitting a state to the Union granted the state certain public lands and established some very ambiguous conditions on the state's subsequent disposition of these lands. This federal statute also required the new state to write those exact same conditions into its state constitution.
One hundred years later, a state statute dealing with the sale of these public lands was challenged in a state court lawsuit on the ground that it was inconsistent with the conditions contained in the federal statute and with the provisions of the state constitution that exactly copy the conditions contained in the federal statute.
The trial court decision in this case was appealed to the state supreme court. In its opinion, the state supreme court dealt at length with the ambiguous language of the federal statute and with cases interpreting identical language in federal statutes admitting other states to the union. The state supreme court opinion did not discuss the similar provisions of the state constitution, but it did hold that the challenged state statute is invalid because it is "inconsistent with the language of the federal statute and therefore is inconsistent with the identical provisions of our state constitution."
If the losing party in the state supreme court seeks review of the decision of that court in the United States Supreme Court, how should the United States Supreme Court proceed?

choices.A: The court should accept the case for review and determine the validity of the interpretation of the federal statute if it is an important and substantial question.
choices.B: The court should ask the state supreme court to indicate more clearly whether it relied on the state constitutional provision in rendering its decision.
choices.C: The court should decline to review the case because a decision by a state supreme court concerning the proper disposition of state public lands is not reviewable by the United States Supreme Court.
choices.D: The court should decline to review the case on the ground that the decision of the state supreme court rests on an adequate and independent state ground.

questions.explanation:
The Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) has appellate jurisdiction to review decisions issued by lower federal courts and the highest state courts that concern important and substantial issues of federal law. But SCOTUS has no jurisdiction to review a state court decision that is supported by state-law grounds that are both:

  • adequate – when state law completely resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and
  • independent – when the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its decision.

Here, a state statute dealing with the sale of certain public lands was challenged in state court and held to be inconsistent with a federal statute and the state constitution (adequate state grounds). But the state supreme court's decision relied on federal case law that interpreted identical language in other federal statutes (no independent state grounds) (Choice D). Therefore, SCOTUS should review the state supreme court's interpretation if it is an important and substantial question.

(Choice B) The state supreme court explicitly stated that it relied on federal case law, so no clarification is needed. But even if the grounds for the state court's decision were unclear, SCOTUS would not ask the state court for clarification. Instead, SCOTUS would assume that the state court used federal law to reach its decision, rule on the federal issue, and remand the case to state court to resolve any remaining state-law issues.

(Choice C) SCOTUS can review a state supreme court decision—even if it involves the proper disposition of state public lands—as long as that decision was not based on adequate and independent state-law grounds.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court has no jurisdiction to review a state court decision based on an adequate state-law ground that completely resolves the case independent of federal law.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1040–41 (1983) (explaining when a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds).
  • 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 44 (2019) (listing the rules to determine whether a decision rests on adequate and independent state grounds).
questions.zh-question:
一项接纳某州加入联邦的联邦法规授予该州某些公共土地，并对该州后续处置这些土地设立了一些非常模糊的条件。该联邦法规还要求这个新成立的州将这些完全相同的条件写入其州宪法。

一百年后，一项关于出售这些公共土地的州法规在州法院的诉讼中受到质疑，理由是该法规与联邦法规中所包含的条件不一致，也与州宪法中完全照搬联邦法规条件的条款不一致。

该案的初审法院判决被上诉至州最高法院。在其判决意见中，州最高法院详细论述了该联邦法规的模糊语言，以及解释接纳其他州加入联邦的联邦法规中相同语言的案例。州最高法院的判决意见没有讨论州宪法中的类似条款，但它确实裁定，被质疑的州法规无效，因为其“与联邦法规的语言不一致，因此也与我们州宪法中的相同条款不一致。”

如果州最高法院的败诉方寻求 United States Supreme Court 对该法院判决的复审，United States Supreme Court 应如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 如果这是一个重要且实质性的问题，法院应受理此案进行复审，并对联邦法规解释的有效性作出裁定。
zh-choices.B: 法院应要求州最高法院更清楚地表明其在作出判决时是否依赖了州宪法条款。
zh-choices.C: 法院应拒绝复审此案，因为州最高法院关于州公共土地适当处置的判决，United States Supreme Court 无权复审。
zh-choices.D: 法院应以州最高法院的判决基于充分且独立的州法律依据为由，拒绝复审此案。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州最高法院表面提到联邦法，但其实有没有真正落在独立且充分的州法根据（adequate and independent state grounds）上，决定美国最高法院能不能审。

三秒认题路径：

州高院判了 → 有联邦问题 → 但有州法根 → 独立吗 → 能否受理

核心法律规则

美国最高法院（SCOTUS（Supreme Court of the United States））可以复核州最高法院判决中的联邦法问题，但前提是该判决不是建立在充分且独立的州法根据（adequate and independent state grounds）上。adequate 的考场意思是：州法自己就足以把案子判完，联邦法再怎么改也不影响结果。

independent 的考场意思是：州法院不是靠联邦法才得出结论；如果它其实靠的是联邦法，SCOTUS 就可以抓住这个联邦问题继续审。这里州高院一边分析联邦成州法时沿用的语言，一边直接说州法与联邦法“语言一致”，所以它没有真正切断联邦法依赖。

核心判例： Michigan v. Long —— 州法院若没有清楚表明自己只靠州法，联邦法院可推定它在处理联邦问题，从而获得审查权。

思维导图

先看：州最高法院这份判决，SCOTUS 能不能碰？
1.有没有联邦问题（federal issue）？
有：法院讨论了联邦成州法的同源语言，说明不是纯州法小案。
2.有没有充分且独立的州法根据（adequate and independent state grounds）？
adequate 州法能单独撑住结论：这一步本题表面上像是有。
independent 真正卡死点：州高院其实在用联邦法解释同样措辞，没把州法和联邦法分开。
卡死点：不是“有州法字样”就算独立；只要判决还在靠联邦法解释，SCOTUS 就能审。
结论→ 受理并判断联邦法解释是否“重要且重大”
答案：A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州法院已经提到州宪法，而且州公地处置看起来像纯州事务，所以美国最高法院不能碰。

但考试真正问的是：这份判决是不是已经被独立的州法根据彻底撑住；如果州法院还是靠联邦法解释同样的文字，SCOTUS 仍能审联邦问题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里州高院长篇讨论联邦成州法的同样措辞，说明判决并非完全独立于联邦法；因此 SCOTUS 可以受理并审查该联邦解释是否重要且重大。

❌ 概念混淆 | 误把含糊当需澄清

✕ B: 题干已看出州高院在用联邦法，ask the state 不是这题的走法。

❌ 事实误判 | 误当纯州公地案

✕ C: 不是因为是州公地就完全不可审，关键是有没有联邦问题卡住。

❌ 法律适用 | 独立性判断错位

✕ D: 州法看似够用，但州高院没有把联邦法彻底切开，adequate 不能单独挡住 SCOTUS。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看州法能不能独立结案，再盯州法院有没有真正摆脱联邦法依赖。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先问充分，再问独立；只要州高院还在借联邦法解释同一句话，SCOTUS 就可能进场。口诀也可记成：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，用来提醒自己先看法定例外，再看能不能立刻上诉。
