questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute provides that the United States Supreme Court has authority to review any case filed in a United States court of appeals, even if that case has not yet been decided by the court of appeals.
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), an agency in the executive branch of the federal government, issued an important environmental rule. Although the rule had not yet been enforced against them, companies that would be adversely affected by the rule filed a petition for review of the rule in a court of appeals, seeking a declaration that the rule was invalid solely because it was beyond the statutory authority of the EPA. The companies made no constitutional claim. A statute specifically provides for direct review of EPA rules by a court of appeals without any initial action in a district court.
The companies have filed a petition for a writ of certiorari in the Supreme Court requesting immediate review of this case by the Supreme Court before the court of appeals has actually decided the case. The EPA acknowledges that the case is important enough to warrant Supreme Court review and that it should be decided promptly, but it asks the Supreme Court to dismiss the petition on jurisdictional grounds.
What is the best constitutional argument in support of the EPA's request?

choices.A: Article III precludes federal courts from reviewing the validity of any federal agency rule in any proceeding other than an action to enforce the rule.
choices.B: Article III provides that all federal cases, except those within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, must be initiated by an action in a federal district court.
choices.C: The case is appellate in nature, but it is beyond the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, because Article III states that its jurisdiction extends only to cases arising under the Constitution.
choices.D: The case is not within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court as defined by Article III, and it is not a proper subject of that court's appellate jurisdiction because it has not yet been decided by any lower court.

questions.explanation:
Article III of the Constitution states that the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has both:

  • original jurisdiction – the authority to directly review (1) cases involving an ambassador, public minister, or consul and (2) cases in which a state is a party and
  • appellate jurisdiction – the authority to overturn, modify, or affirm a decision made by a lower federal court or a state's highest court in all other cases falling within federal judicial power.

Here, the companies filed a petition for a writ of certiorari requesting that SCOTUS immediately review their case against the EPA. But the case is not within SCOTUS's original jurisdiction as narrowly defined by Article III. And since the case has not yet been decided by a lower court—ie, there is no decision being appealed from—it is not a proper subject of SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. Accordingly, that is the best constitutional argument in support of the EPA's request.

(Choice A) Article III allows federal courts to review the validity of a federal rule in a proceeding other than an action to enforce the rule. For example, federal courts may issue a declaratory judgment that a rule is invalid before it has been enforced if the plaintiff faces imminent harm.

(Choice B) Under Article III, Congress has broad power to regulate the original and appellate jurisdiction of lower federal courts. As a result, a federal case can be initiated by an action in a U.S. court of appeals rather than a U.S. district court if authorized by Congress.

(Choice C) SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction extends to all cases arising under the Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (as seen here). But this case is not appellate in nature since there is no lower court decision to review.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has original jurisdiction in (1) cases involving an ambassador, public minister, or consul and (2) cases in which a state is a party. But in all other cases, SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction requires a lower court decision.

📚 References
  • Balt. & Ohio R.R. Co. v. Interstate Com. Comm'n, 215 U.S. 216, 224–25 (1909) (explaining that SCOTUS has original jurisdiction in limited circumstances and that appellate jurisdiction requires a lower court decision).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 453 (2019) (defining original and appellate jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规规定，美国最高法院有权审查向美国上诉法院提起的任何案件，即使该案件尚未由上诉法院裁决。

环境保护局（EPA），作为联邦政府行政部门的一个机构，发布了一项重要的环境法规。尽管该法规尚未对它们强制执行，但会受到该法规不利影响的公司向上诉法院提交了审查该法规的申请，请求宣告该法规无效，其唯一理由是该法规超出了EPA的法定权限。这些公司没有提出任何宪法上的主张。一项法规明确规定，EPA的法规可由上诉法院直接审查，而无需在地区法院提起初步诉讼。

这些公司已向最高法院提交了调卷令申请，请求在最高法院在上诉法院实际裁决该案之前立即对其进行审查。EPA承认该案的重要性足以值得最高法院审查，并且应迅速作出裁决，但它请求最高法院以管辖权为由驳回该申请。

支持EPA请求的最佳宪法论据是什么？

zh-choices.A: Article III禁止联邦法院在执行该法规的诉讼之外的任何程序中审查任何联邦机构法规的有效性。
zh-choices.B: Article III规定，除最高法院初审管辖权内的案件外，所有联邦案件都必须通过在联邦地区法院提起诉讼来启动。
zh-choices.C: 该案本质上是上诉案件，但它超出了最高法院的上诉管辖权，因为Article III规定其管辖权仅延伸至根据宪法产生的案件。
zh-choices.D: 该案不属于Article III所定义的最高法院初审管辖权范围，也不是该法院上诉管辖权的适当标的，因为它尚未经过任何下级法院的裁决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial review in operation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：最高法院（Supreme Court）能不能在没有任何下级法院判决时，直接把一个案子拿来做上诉管辖（appellate jurisdiction）审查。

三秒认题路径：

无下级判决 → 不是原始管辖 → 不能直接上诉 → 选 D

核心法律规则

原始管辖（original jurisdiction）考场意思：最高法院只有在“外交官、领事”或“州是当事方”这两类案子里，才可以直接受理。其他案子默认走上诉管辖（appellate jurisdiction），也就是先有下级法院判决，再谈最高法院审查。

上诉管辖（appellate jurisdiction）考场意思：不是“案子重要就能上最高法院”，而是必须先有一个可被复审的决定。没有下级法院已经作出的裁判，就没有东西可“上诉”。

核心判例： Balt. & Ohio R.R. Co. v. Interstate Com. Comm'n — 说明最高法院原始管辖很窄，通常的上诉管辖要建立在下级法院决定之上。

思维导图

先看：最高法院现在有没有“可审的下级法院判决”？
YES如果已经有上诉法院或州最高法院的判决，才进入正常appellate jurisdiction。
NO题干这里没有任何下级法院决定，只有公司想让最高法院“抢先审”。
卡死点：没有被上诉的裁判，就没有最高法院的普通上诉入口。
再看：它是不是最高法院的原始管辖案？
YES只限ambassador / public minister / consul，或state is a party。
NO本题只是公司挑战 EPA 规则，不属于这两类。
结论怎么落地？
既不是原始管辖，也不是已存在判决上的上诉管辖，所以不能直接让最高法院受理。
答案锁定：D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：EPA 规则很重要，法院又说应当尽快解决，所以最高法院应该可以直接接手。

但考试真正问的是：程序入口对不对，不是案子值不值得快点处理。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的陷阱就是把“重要”偷换成“可直接上诉”。在 MBE 里，重要性不能替代下级法院判决，也不能把普通上诉管辖变成原始管辖。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最关键的 before the court of appeals has actually decided the case 说明没有可上诉的下级判决，最高法院既无原始管辖，也不能直接行使上诉管辖。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把规则争议当成只能 enforcement 才能审，declaratory judgment 也能先行挑战。

❌ 事实误判 | 起诉层级偷换

✕ B: 乱说所有联邦案都先去地区法院，题干明明允许直接在上诉法院起案。

❌ 法律适用 | 宪法范围误判

✕ C: 把 arising under 当成最高法院可直接受理的理由，但这题卡在没有下级判决。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否有终局判决，再看是否落入原始管辖；没有就别急着谈“重要性”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：最高法院先看门，先问是不是原始管辖，再问有没有下级法院判决；没有判决，就别硬塞进上诉管辖。

记住这句：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 主要说的是法定中间上诉例外，不是“只要重要就能越级上最高法院”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Distinguish original from appellate jurisdiction

keywords.text: has not yet been decided by the court of appeals

reason.en: Without a lower-court decision, the Supreme Court has nothing to review through appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 没有下级法院裁决，最高法院就没有可通过上诉管辖权审查的对象。

keywords.text: direct review of EPA rules by a court of appeals

label.zh: 法定上诉法院直接审查

reason.en: Congress may authorize initial review of an agency rule in a court of appeals.
reason.zh: 国会可以授权上诉法院直接初审行政机关规则。

keywords.text: petition for a writ of certiorari

label.en: request for discretionary Supreme Court review
label.zh: 最高法院酌情审查申请

reason.en: Certiorari invokes appellate review and therefore ordinarily requires a lower-court decision.
reason.zh: 调卷令申请启动上诉审查，因此通常要求已有下级法院裁决。

keywords.text: before the court of appeals has actually decided the case

reason.en: This timing fact makes the requested Supreme Court review constitutionally nonappellate.
reason.zh: 这一时点事实使所请求的最高法院审查不具备宪法上的上诉性质。

reason.en: The EPA challenges the Supreme Court's constitutional authority to hear the case at this stage.
reason.zh: EPA质疑最高法院在当前阶段审理该案的宪法权限。

A.text: other than an action to enforce the rule

reason.en: Article III does not categorically restrict pre-enforcement judicial review of agency rules.
reason.zh: 第三条并未绝对禁止对行政规则进行执法前司法审查。

B.text: must be initiated by an action in a federal district court

label.zh: 必须由地区法院启动的主张

reason.en: Congress may authorize proceedings to begin directly in a federal court of appeals.
reason.zh: 国会可以授权案件直接在联邦上诉法院启动。

label.zh: 错误认定的上诉程序地位

reason.en: The case is not yet appellate because no lower court has issued a decision.
reason.zh: 由于尚无下级法院裁决，该案目前并不具有上诉性质。

C.text: only to cases arising under the Constitution

label.zh: 过度狭窄的联邦问题管辖

reason.en: Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction also encompasses cases arising under federal statutes and treaties.
reason.zh: 最高法院的上诉管辖权还涵盖依据联邦法律和条约产生的案件。

label.zh: 不属于宪法规定的初审管辖

reason.en: The dispute involves neither a specified foreign official nor a state as a party.
reason.zh: 该争议既不涉及特定外国官员，也没有州作为当事方。

D.text: not a proper subject of that court's appellate jurisdiction

reason.en: Appellate jurisdiction requires an existing decision that the Supreme Court can review.
reason.zh: 上诉管辖权要求已有可供最高法院审查的裁决。

D.text: has not yet been decided by any lower court

label.zh: 无可审查的下级法院裁决

reason.en: This is the controlling fact preventing immediate Supreme Court appellate review.
reason.zh: 这是阻止最高法院立即进行上诉审查的决定性事实。

highlights.text: even if that case has not yet been decided by the court of appeals

label.zh: 下级法院裁决前的审查

reason.en: This statutory authorization conflicts with the constitutional requirement that appellate review follow a lower-court decision.
reason.zh: 该法定授权与上诉审查须以已有下级法院裁决为前提的宪法要求冲突。

highlights.text: The companies made no constitutional claim.

reason.en: A statutory federal claim still falls within federal judicial power, so the absence of a constitutional claim is not jurisdictionally fatal.
reason.zh: 联邦制定法主张仍属于联邦司法权范围，因此没有宪法主张并不导致管辖权缺失。

highlights.text: A statute specifically provides for direct review of EPA rules by a court of appeals without any initial action in a district court.

label.zh: 有效的上诉法院直接审查

reason.en: This eliminates the distractor claiming that every federal case must begin in a district court.
reason.zh: 这排除了所有联邦案件都必须始于地区法院这一干扰项。

highlights.text: requesting immediate review of this case by the Supreme Court before the court of appeals has actually decided the case

label.zh: 过早请求最高法院审查

reason.en: Because no lower-court decision exists, the request cannot invoke the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction.
reason.zh: 由于不存在下级法院裁决，该请求无法启动最高法院的上诉管辖权。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A wastewater treatment facility was fined for violating a state law regarding the discharge of pollutants into water sources. The facility challenged the fine in state court on the basis that the state law conflicted with federal law. In the state court's opinion, which sided with the facility, the court analyzed the state law in light of federal law regarding pollution and the water source where the pollutants were discharged but failed to clearly indicate the basis for its decision. On appeal, the decision was affirmed per curiam by the highest court of the state. The state appealed the decision to the U.S. Supreme Court.
Which of the following would be the most likely reason for the U.S. Supreme Court to review this case?

choices.A: Federal law would consider the discharge from the facility to be illegal pollution.
choices.B: The state-court decision incorrectly applied state law.
choices.C: The state-court decision relied on federal law.
choices.D: The U.S. Supreme Court is required to hear the case.

questions.explanation:
Jurisdiction of United States Supreme Court

(render decision)

(affirm, reverse, modify decision)

State Supreme Court
State Intermediate Court
U.S. District Court
State Trial Court
Case involves (1) ambassador, public minister, consul or (2) state is party
All other cases

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has discretion to review a judgment issued by a state's highest court that turns on federal law. But SCOTUS must decline to review a state-court judgment based on state grounds that are:

  • adequate – the state grounds fully resolve the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and
  • independent – it is clear from the opinion that the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its conclusion.

Here, the state court's decision, which was affirmed per curiam by the state's highest court, analyzed the state law in light of federal law. However, the court did not clearly indicate whether it relied on federal law or state law to reach its decision. Therefore, the most likely reason for SCOTUS to review this case would be that the state-court decision relied on federal law.

(Choice A) Even if federal law would consider the discharge from the facility to be illegal pollution, the wastewater treatment plant was fined for violating state law. And if the state judgment had been supported on state grounds that were independent and adequate, then SCOTUS would be unable to hear the matter.

(Choice B) SCOTUS may review a highest state-court judgment that turns on federal law. However, it must decline jurisdiction to review decisions involving the application of state law.

(Choice D) SCOTUS has discretion to review a highest state-court judgment that turns on federal law. But it is not required to review such decisions on appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

SCOTUS has discretion to review a judgement issued by a state's highest court that turns on federal law. But it must decline to review a state-court judgment based on state grounds that are adequate and independent.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (holding that a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds only if the state court makes a plain statement to that effect).
  • 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 44 (2019) (explaining the plain statement rule).
questions.zh-question:
一家污水处理设施因违反州法律向水源排放污染物而被罚款。该设施在州法院对罚款提出异议，理由是该州法律与联邦法律冲突。州法院的判决支持了该设施，判决中参照联邦污染法律和污染物排放水源分析了州法律，但未能明确指出其判决依据。上诉后，州最高法院以 *per curiam* 意见维持原判。该州随后向美国最高法院上诉。
以下哪项是美国最高法院审查此案最可能的原因？

zh-choices.A: 联邦法律会认为该设施的排放是非法污染。
zh-choices.B: 州法院的判决错误地适用了州法律。
zh-choices.C: 州法院的判决依赖于联邦法律。
zh-choices.D: 美国最高法院必须审理此案。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州最高法院判决如果依赖联邦法，美国最高法院就可能审查；如果只是独立且充分的州法理由，就不能管。

三秒认题路径：

终局州判决 → 看联邦法 → 查独立州法 → 仍可审查？ → 选依赖联邦法

核心法律规则

美国最高法院对州最高法院的判决有上诉审查权，但前提是该判决转而依赖联邦法（federal law）。如果州法院是靠独立且充分的州法依据（adequate and independent state grounds）作出结论，SCOTUS 就不能碰。

考试上最重要的不是州法院有没有提到联邦法，而是它到底靠什么赢/输。只要判决理由没有清楚说“我完全只靠州法”，就会触发 plain statement rule：默认它可能依赖联邦法，SCOTUS 就可能审查。

核心判例： Michigan v. Long - 州最高法院没有明确表明自己只靠州法时，联邦最高法院可以推定其判决涉及联邦法，从而行使审查权。

思维导图

州最高法院判决，SCOTUS 能不能审？
先问 1：是不是终局州判决？
是终局判决，才进入联邦审查问题；本题不是原审法院的普通中间裁定。
再问 2：判决是靠州法还是联邦法？
如果州法院明确写明只靠州法，且州法理由独立且充分，SCOTUS 不能审。
如果州法院混着讲，又没说清楚只靠州法，就按 plain statement rule 处理。
卡死点：
本题州法院拿联邦污染法来分析，但没有清楚表明只依州法，所以结论是：可能依赖联邦法。
终点：SCOTUS 可审查 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然州法院最后是支持工厂，题目是不是在问联邦污染法到底怎么解释，或者州法本身对不对。

但考试真正问的是：这份州判决有没有把自己锁进“独立且充分的州法理由”里。它没有说清楚，所以 SCOTUS 还有门可进。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干说州法院“结合联邦污染法”分析，却没清楚说明只靠州法作决定，这正是 可能依赖联邦法 的信号，所以 SCOTUS 可能审查。

❌ 事实误判 | 污染结论偷换

✕ A: 把联邦污染是否合法当成审查理由，错看成实体污染争议了。

❌ 法律适用 | 州法独立误判

✕ B: 只说州法错了不够，关键是它有没有独立且充分地支撑结果。

❌ 概念混淆 | 强制受理误判

✕ D: 把 required 当成必须受理，但最高法院这里只有裁量权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“州判决是不是靠联邦法”，再看有没有独立且充分的州法理由。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先看州法能不能单独站住；站不住，又提到联邦法，SCOTUS 就可能进场。 这类题先找 adequate and independent state grounds，再想 plain statement rule。

reason.en: Establishes a final state judgment while preserving the ambiguity in its legal basis.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress recently enacted a statute imposing severe criminal penalties on anyone engaged in trading in the stock market who, in the course of that trading, takes "unfair advantage" of other investors who are also trading in the stock market. The statute does not define the term "unfair advantage." There have been no prosecutions under this new statute.
The members of an association of law school professors that is dedicated to increasing the clarity of the language used in criminal statutes believe that this statute is unconstitutionally vague. Neither the association nor any of its members is currently engaged in, or intends in the future to engage in, trading in the stock market.
The association and its members bring suit against the Attorney General of the United States in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of this statute on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
May the federal court determine the merits of this suit?

choices.A: No, because a suit for an injunction against enforcement of a criminal statute may not be brought in federal court at any time prior to a bona fide effort to enforce that statute.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating this statute that is adequate to ensure that the suit presents an Article III controversy.
choices.C: Yes, because the plaintiffs seek real relief of a conclusive nature—an injunction against enforcement of this statute.
choices.D: Yes, because the suit involves a dispute over the constitutionality of a federal statute.

questions.explanation:
Article III only allows federal courts to determine the merits of actual cases or controversies. The doctrine of standing ensures that this requirement is met by requiring the plaintiff to show that he/she has a personal stake in the outcome of the case. This exists when the plaintiff has suffered an injury-in-fact—ie, concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent—that was caused by the challenged conduct and is redressable by a favorable decision.

Here, the association and its members sued in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of the stock market statute. But the statute has not caused these plaintiffs an injury-in-fact because neither is currently engaged in, or intends to engage in, stock market trading (no actual or imminent harm). This means that the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating the statute that would satisfy Article III's case-or-controversy requirement. As a result, the court cannot determine the merits of their suit.

(Choice A) Even if a criminal statute has not been enforced, a suit for an injunction to prevent such enforcement may be brought in federal court if the plaintiff shows that the statute poses an immediate threat of harm (not seen here).

(Choice C) The injunction would provide real and conclusive relief. But the federal court does not have the power to issue an injunction in a suit that does not meet the case-or-controversy requirement (as seen here).

(Choice D) Federal courts have subject-matter jurisdiction over suits involving the constitutionality of federal statutes. But the court cannot hear the merits of such a suit when, as here, the plaintiffs lack standing to assert their constitutional challenge.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of standing, an injury-in-fact exists when the plaintiff has suffered concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent.

📚 References
  • Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560–61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).
questions.zh-question:
国会最近颁布了一项法规，对任何在股票市场交易中，利用其他同样在进行股票交易的投资者的“不公平优势”的人，处以严厉的刑事处罚。该法规未定义“不公平优势”这一术语。目前尚无根据此新法规提起的诉讼。

一个致力于提高刑事法语言清晰度的法学院教授协会的成员们认为，该法规因含糊不清而违宪。该协会及其任何成员目前没有，也无意在将来从事股票市场交易。

该协会及其成员向美国联邦地区法院对美国司法部长提起诉讼，以该法规违宪为由，请求法院颁布禁止执行该法规的禁令。

联邦法院能否就此案的实体问题作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为在善意执行某刑事法规之前，任何时候都不得向联邦法院提起旨在禁止执行该法规的禁令之诉。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为原告在宣告该法规无效一事上不具有充分的利益，以确保该诉讼构成 Article III 所规定的争议。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为原告寻求的是具有确定性的实际救济——一项禁止执行该法规的禁令。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该诉讼涉及一项关于联邦法规合宪性的争议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原告没有 诉讼资格（standing），因为他们没有真实或迫近的 injury-in-fact，所以联邦法院不能审实体。

三秒认题路径：

没人会被罚 → 没现实伤害 → 没 standing → 不能审实体 → 选 B

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住三件事

诉讼资格（standing） 是 Article III（案件或争议） 的门槛，考场意思：先看原告能不能进门，不是先看法条好不好看。

它通常要有三步：injury-in-fact（事实损害）、因果关系、可救济性。考场意思：你得先真的被打到，法院才会管。

这里原告既没有正在交易，也没有打算交易，所以没有实际或迫近的伤害；就算法条可能很模糊，也不能靠“我觉得它不清楚”直接把案件推进实体审理。

核心判例： Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife — 站位规则锁死：没有 concrete and particularized 的现实或迫近损害，就没有 standing。

思维导图

先问：原告有 Article III standing 吗？
Yes有 injury-in-fact，而且是 concrete、particularized、actual / imminent
No 本题原告不交易、也不打算交易，只有抽象不满
卡死点：没有真实或迫近伤害 → 没 standing → 法院不能审实体
再问：能不能靠“想阻止执行”补上门槛？
No 光有 injunction（禁令） 请求不够，先得有可审的案件或争议
结论：联邦法院要先挡在门口
→ 没 standing，就直接选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：法条写得很模糊，又是刑事罚则，所以法院应该先帮他们把 unconstitutional vagueness 处理掉。

但考试真正问的是：这批原告根本没被这条法条现实威胁到，先得过 standing 这一关。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 没有正在交易，也没有打算交易，所以没有 actual 或 imminent injury；没 standing，就不能进入实体审查。

❌ 法律适用 | 强制前置误判

✕ A: 把起诉门槛说成一定要先 bona fide effort，其实这题卡的是 standing，不是执法时点。

❌ 概念混淆 | 禁令可救误判

✕ C: 看到 real relief 就心动，但先没有案件或争议，法院连禁令都不能发。

❌ 事实误判 | 联邦审理偷换

✕ D: 有联邦法不等于能直接审实体；原告没受影响，还是进不了门。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看原告有没有现实伤害，再决定联邦法院能不能碰实体。

考场速记

记住一句：standing 先过门槛，injury-in-fact 要真实或迫近；没被打到，就别急着谈宪法。

口诀：Lujan 先看三件事，injury、因果、可救济；少了第一项，后面都白搭。

B.text: do not have an interest in invalidating this statute

C.text: real relief of a conclusive nature

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute requires the National Bureau of Standards to establish minimum quality standards for all beer sold in the United States. The statute also provides that public hearings must precede adoption of the standards, and that once they are adopted, the standards will be subject to judicial review. While the proposed standards have not yet been announced, several Bureau officials have publicly expressed opinions indicating a belief that pasteurized beer is safer than unpasteurized beer. However, these officials have not stated whether they intend to include a pasteurization requirement in the standards.
A brewery that produces unpasteurized beer is concerned that, after the appropriate proceedings, the Bureau may adopt quality standards that will prohibit the sale of unpasteurized beer. The brewery has sued in federal district court to enjoin the Bureau from adopting standards that would prohibit the sale of unpasteurized beer.
How should the district court proceed with the suit?

choices.A: Determine whether the Bureau could reasonably believe that pasteurization is the safest process by which to brew beer and, if so, refuse to issue the injunction against the Bureau.
choices.B: Determine whether the process used by the brewery is as safe as pasteurization and, if so, issue the injunction against the Bureau.
choices.C: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and dismiss it, because it does not involve a justiciable case or controversy.
choices.D: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit at this time and stay the action until the Bureau has actually issued beer-quality standards.

questions.explanation:
Justiciability
(suitability for judicial resolution)
Case or controversy Prohibits advisory opinions under three doctrines:
  • Standing – plaintiff must allege injury-in-fact caused by challenged action & redressable by remedy sought
  • Ripeness – claim must present actual controversy involving past injury or present threat of injury
  • Mootness – claim must be unresolved
Adequate & independent state grounds SCOTUS cannot review final state court judgment that rests on adequate & independent state grounds
Political question Court cannot hear case if issue presented:
  • is reserved for executive/legislative branches or
  • lacks judicially manageable standards for resolution
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

A federal court should not proceed with a suit unless it is justiciable—ie, appropriate for judicial resolution—based on the following Article III requirements: (1) case or controversy, (2) no adequate and independent state grounds, and (3) no political questions. The case-or-controversy requirement is met if the plaintiff has standing—ie, suffered an injury-in-fact that was caused by the defendant and is redressable by the court. An injury-in-fact exists if the plaintiff alleges actual, or an immediate threat of, harm. Therefore, a court should dismiss a suit that is:

  • unripe – the suit is based on the mere potential for, or future threat of, harm or
  • moot – the suit no longer presents a live (ie, actual) controversy for the court to resolve.

Here, the brewery filed suit in federal district court to enjoin the Bureau from adopting standards that would prohibit the brewery from selling unpasteurized beer. But this suit does not involve a justiciable case or controversy because the Bureau has not adopted such standards (no actual harm) and public hearings that must precede the adoption have yet to occur (no imminent harm). Therefore, the court should refuse to adjudicate the merits of this unripe suit and dismiss it.

(Choices A & B) Since this suit is not justiciable, the court cannot consider its merits—eg, whether (1) the Bureau could reasonably believe that pasteurization is the safest process or (2) the brewery's process is as safe as pasteurization.

(Choice D) A federal court can stay (ie, suspend) a suit to (1) force a party to comply with a court order or (2) protect a party's rights. However, a federal court must dismiss a suit when, as here, it does not present a justiciable case or controversy.

📌 Educational Objective

Article III limits the jurisdiction of federal courts to justiciable cases or controversies. This requires proof that the plaintiff has suffered an injury-in-fact—ie, an actual, or immediate threat of, harm. Therefore, a federal court must dismiss a suit involving future or resolved harm.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).
  • Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规要求国家标准局（National Bureau of Standards）为在美国销售的所有啤酒制定最低质量标准。该法规还规定，在通过这些标准之前必须举行公开听证会，并且一旦通过，这些标准将接受司法审查。尽管拟议的标准尚未公布，但该局的几名官员已公开发表意见，表示他们相信巴氏杀菌啤酒比未经巴氏杀菌的啤酒更安全。然而，这些官员并未说明他们是否打算在标准中加入巴氏杀菌的要求。

一家生产未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的啤酒厂担心，在经过适当程序后，该局可能会通过禁止销售未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的质量标准。该啤酒厂已向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，请求法院发布禁令，禁止该局通过会禁止销售未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的标准。

地区法院应如何处理此案？

zh-choices.A: 裁定该局是否可以合理地认为巴氏杀菌是酿造啤酒最安全的流程，如果可以，则拒绝向该局发出禁令。
zh-choices.B: 裁定该啤酒厂使用的流程是否与巴氏杀菌同样安全，如果是，则向该局发出禁令。
zh-choices.C: 拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决并驳回诉讼，因为该案不涉及可诉的案件或争议。
zh-choices.D: 在此时拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决，并中止诉讼程序，直到该局实际发布了啤酒质量标准。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原告只是担心将来可能被禁止卖未巴氏杀菌啤酒，这种“还没发生、也不够迫近”的担心，不能构成 可裁判争议（case or controversy）。

三秒认题路径：

还没出标准 → 只是担心未来 → 没有现实伤害 → 不成熟（unripe） → 直接驳回

核心法律规则

联邦法院只能审理 可裁判争议（justiciable case or controversy）；考场意思：现在必须已经有真实争端，或者至少有马上要来的伤害，不是纯猜测。

成熟（ripeness） 的考场意思：争议还没“长到能判”的程度，法院现在去讲未来政策会不会伤你，太早了。

本题里，标准还没公布，公开听证也还没开始，啤酒厂只是担心以后可能被限制，所以没有 现实或迫近伤害（actual or immediate threat of harm）。

核心判例：Texas v. United States 说明只有未来威胁太抽象时，案件就是 未成熟（unripe），法院应先拒绝进入实体审理。

思维导图

先问：现在有没有法院能判的真实争议？
否： 标准还没出台 → 没有实际伤害 → 只有未来担心 → 卡死点：unripe，现在不能判
是： 再看是否能救济 → 才进入实体审理
本题结论： 直接驳回 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想： Bureau 官员都说过 pasteurized beer 更安全，法院是不是可以先阻止他们？

但考试真正问的是：现在有没有已经发生、或者马上会发生的法律伤害；这里连标准都没正式出台，听证也还没开，还是“猜未来”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的市场风险会不会吓人」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 标准尚未公布，而且听证都没开始，只有将来可能受影响的担心，所以没有现实争议，必须直接驳回。

❌ 法律适用 | 未来风险误判

✕ A: 把未来安全判断当成现在可判的争议了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 先发救济误判

✕ B: 想先比谁的工艺更安全，但法院连实体都还不能进。

❌ 事实误判 | 误当已有裁定

✕ D: 这里不是先有标准再等上诉，而是标准根本还没出台。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先看有没有真实伤害，再判断是不是只是将来可能受影响。

考场速记

记住一句：没有现实或迫近伤害，就先别急着进法院。本题抓的是 ripeness，不是谁更有道理。

label.zh: 第三条案件或争议要求

highlights.text: public hearings must precede adoption of the standards

label.zh: 尚未完成的强制机构程序

reason.en: The required proceedings make adoption of any harmful standard non-imminent.

highlights.text: the proposed standards have not yet been announced

highlights.text: may adopt quality standards that will prohibit the sale of unpasteurized beer

reason.en: The brewery challenges only a possible future prohibition, making the claim unripe.
reason.zh: 啤酒厂质疑的只是未来可能出现的禁令，因此诉求尚未成熟。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The federal parole commission denied a federal prisoner's request for parole based on the commission's parole guidelines. The prisoner subsequently filed a class action against the commission in federal court, challenging the facial validity of the commission's parole guidelines on the basis that the guidelines violate federal law. After the court certified the class action, the prisoner was released from prison. The commission has moved to dismiss the case.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because an actual case or controversy exists for the court to decide.
choices.B: No, because the prisoner's suit is not ripe for decision.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits this type of action in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the prisoner's claim has become moot.

questions.explanation:
Ripeness v. Mootness
Ripe
(too soon) 		Action will not be heard until plaintiff has experienced actual injury or imminent threat thereof
Moot
(too late) 		Action will be dismissed if further proceedings would have no effect unless:
  • plaintiff's harm is capable of repetition yet evading review (eg, pregnancy)
  • defendant voluntarily stops action but can resume it anytime
  • plaintiff is named plaintiff in class action & claims of unnamed plaintiffs are still viable

Article III of the Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide actual cases and controversies—ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. If further legal proceedings would no longer have an effect—often because the plaintiff's harm has been resolved—then an actual case or controversy typically ceases to exist. When this occurs, the plaintiff's claim is typically rendered moot and the case must then be dismissed.

However, one exception to this rule applies when the plaintiff whose claim has become moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action (as seen here). If the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in the class are still viable, then the class action will not be dismissed as moot. That is because, while the named plaintiff's personal claim has become moot, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs' claims.

Here, the prisoner filed a class action in federal court, thereby serving as the named plaintiff. The prisoner's personal claim—that the commission's parole guidelines violate federal law—became moot when he was released from prison. However, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs who have not been released (Choice A). Therefore, the court should deny the commission's motion to dismiss.

(Choice B) For a suit to be ripe for decision, the plaintiff must have experienced a real injury or immediate threat thereof. Here, the prisoner suffered actual harm when the commission denied the prisoner's request for parole, so this suit is ripe for decision.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment prohibits foreign governments and private parties from suing a state in federal court. It does not prohibit private parties from suing the federal government in federal court (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court typically must dismiss a case when the plaintiff's claim becomes moot. However, one exception applies when (1) a plaintiff whose claim is moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action and (2) the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in that class action are still viable.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • U.S. Parole Comm'n v. Geraghty, 445 U.S. 388, 404 (1980) (holding that federal courts must not dismiss a class action when the named plaintiff's claim becomes moot so long as the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs are viable).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 575 (2020) (defining mootness and its exceptions).

联邦假释委员会根据其假释准则，驳回了一名联邦囚犯的假释申请。该囚犯随后在联邦法院对该委员会提起集体诉讼，以该准则违反联邦法律为由，质疑其假释准则的表面有效性。在法院认证该集体诉讼后，该囚犯被释放出狱。该委员会已动议驳回此案。

法院应否批准该动议？

zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该囚犯的诉讼尚未成熟，不宜裁决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：已认证的集体诉讼（certified class action）里，名义原告（named plaintiff）个人请求变成 moot 后，案件会不会因为还有未失效的未具名成员（unnamed plaintiffs）而继续存在。

三秒认题路径：

认证集体诉讼 → 原告出狱 → 个人主张失效 → 看未具名成员 → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

案件或争议（case or controversy）是联邦法院的门票；如果继续审理已经对当事人没有实际影响，个人请求就会变成 moot，通常要驳回。

但如果这个人是已认证集体诉讼的名义原告，只要未具名成员的请求还活着，法院就还有可裁判的争议，所以不能因为名义原告个人出局就直接结案。

ripe 是“现在还太早”，moot 是“已经太晚”；这题里原告先被拒绝假释，已经有实际损害，所以不是 ripeness 问题。

核心判例： U.S. Parole Comm'n v. Geraghty — 名义原告个人请求变 moot 后，只要认证集体诉讼中未具名成员仍有有效主张，案件仍可继续。

思维导图

先问：现在还有没有 actual case or controversy？
1.先看是否 final judgment 终局？这题不是上诉时机题，而是mootness。
2.如果个人请求已经失效，默认要驳回；但certified class action 另算。
3.关键门槛：未具名成员的请求仍有效 → 争议还在 → 不能 dismiss。
4.本题事实链：拒绝假释 → 原告出狱 → 个人请求 moot → 类成员仍在服刑 → 保留争议。
结论：选 A，因为案件没有真正失去司法可裁判性。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：原告已经出狱，自己的请求没了，所以案子当然 moot。

但考试真正问的是：这不是单打独斗的个人诉讼，而是已认证集体诉讼；只要未具名成员还有活着的请求，法院就还能救济。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「原告本人现在还在不在监狱里」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的已认证集体诉讼让未具名成员的请求继续有效，所以名义原告出狱后，法院仍有 case or controversy 可裁判。

❌ 事实误判 | 仍说太早

✕ B: 把 ripeness 搬来，本题已经发生实际损害，不是“还没到时候”。

❌ 法律适用 | 主体对象错位

✕ C: 看到 Eleventh Amendment 就套州政府豁免，但这里被告是联邦机构。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只盯个人失效

✕ D: 只看原告个人 moot，忽略了类成员还在，争议并没真正消失。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定集体诉讼，再问名义原告失效后是否还有成员保留争议，别被个人出狱带跑。

考场速记

记住：moot 不是“人走了就一定结案”，certified class action 里只要未具名成员还活着，案子通常还能继续。

顺口记：actual case or controversy 还在，法院就不该轻易 dismiss。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The National AIDS Prevention and Control Act is a new, comprehensive federal statute that was enacted to deal with the public health crisis caused by the AIDS virus. Congress and the President were concerned that inconsistent lower court rulings with respect to the constitutionality, interpretation, and application of the statute might adversely affect or delay its enforcement and thereby jeopardize the public health. As a result, they included a provision in the statute providing that all legal challenges concerning those matters may be initiated only by filing suit directly in the United States Supreme Court.
Is the provision authorizing direct review of the constitutionality, interpretation, or application of this statute only in the United States Supreme Court constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it denies persons who wish to challenge this statute the equal protection of the laws by requiring them to file suit in a court different from that in which persons who wish to challenge other statutes may file suit.
choices.B: No, because it is inconsistent with the specification in Article III of the original jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court.
choices.C: Yes, because Article III provides that the jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court is subject to such exceptions and such regulations as Congress shall make.
choices.D: Yes, because it is authorized by the Article I power of Congress to enact all laws that are "necessary and proper" to implement the general welfare.

questions.explanation:
SCOTUS jurisdiction
Type Definition Applicability
Original
(Congress cannot adjust) 		Case filed directly in SCOTUS Cases involving either:
  • • ambassador/public minister/consul or
  • • state as party
Appellate
(Congress may limit) 		Case filed after decision by either:
  • • lower federal court or
  • • highest state court
 All other cases by either:
  • • writ of certiorari or
  • • direct appeal (rare)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

Article III gives the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) original jurisdiction—ie, the authority to directly review a case—in two rare circumstances:

  • when a case affects an ambassador, public minister, or consul and
  • when a state is a party to the suit.

Congress cannot expand or restrict SCOTUS's original jurisdiction beyond Article III's specifications (Choice C). Since the statutory provision attempts to do so by authorizing SCOTUS to directly review challenges to the National AIDS Prevention and Control Act, it is unconstitutional.

(Choice A) This provision implicates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment because it treats persons challenging this statute differently than persons challenging other statutes. But since the provision does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class, it likely does not violate this component.

(Choice D) Article I allows Congress to enact laws that are "necessary and proper" (ie, reasonably appropriate) to carry out its enumerated powers—including the power to spend for the public's general welfare. But when doing so, it cannot violate other constitutional provisions (eg, Article III—as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Article III gives the U.S. Supreme Court original jurisdiction over cases (1) that affect an ambassador, public minister, or consul or (2) in which a state is a party. And Congress cannot alter SCOTUS's original jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. 137, 174–76 (1803) (holding that Congress cannot alter the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 453 (2019) (defining original and appellate jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question: 该条款授权仅由 United States Supreme Court 对此法规的合宪性、解释或适用进行直接审查，此条款是否合宪？

zh-choices.B: 否，因为它与 Article III 中关于 United States Supreme Court 初始管辖权的规定不一致。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为 Article III 规定，United States Supreme Court 的管辖权受国会有权制定的例外和规章的约束。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为它得到了国会 Article I 权力的授权，即为实现普遍福祉而制定所有“必要和适当的”法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Jurisdiction Of The Supreme Court

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能把不属于 最高法院原始管辖权（original jurisdiction） 的案件，硬塞进 美国最高法院（SCOTUS） 直接审理。

三秒认题路径：

直接起诉 SCOTUS → 不是原始管辖 → 国会想改 → Article III 卡死 → 选 B

核心法律规则

Article III 对 最高法院原始管辖权（original jurisdiction） 说得很窄，考场意思：只有两类案件能直接起诉到 SCOTUS。第一类是涉及 大使、公使或领事（ambassador, public minister, or consul） 的案件；第二类是 州作为当事人（state as a party） 的案件。

其他案件都走 上诉管辖权（appellate jurisdiction），考场意思：可以经过下级联邦法院或州最高法院，再按法定方式进到 SCOTUS。国会 不能把本来不在原始管辖里的案件，改成必须直接进 SCOTUS。

核心判例： Marbury v. Madison — 国会不能改写宪法给 SCOTUS 设定的原始管辖范围。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 终局判决（final judgment） 之后的普通上诉？
不是。题干是想让所有挑战 直接 进 SCOTUS，走的是“改管辖”而不是普通上诉。
再问：这是不是 Article III 允许的 原始管辖？
只限两类。 大使 / 公使 / 领事 或 州是当事人
最后卡死点：国会能不能把一般联邦法挑战也塞进原始管辖？
不能。Article III 已经把范围写死了，国会无权扩张。
结论：这个条款违宪，答案选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然国会是为了公共健康、又想提高效率，那就能让 SCOTUS 直接管。

但考试真正问的是：管辖权 能不能改，不是政策好不好。这题看的是“宪法有没有给这个入口”，不是“立法目的重不重要”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干要把一般法条挑战都交给 直接起诉 SCOTUS，但 Article III 只给了两类原始管辖，国会不能加码。

❌ 概念混淆 | 平等保护误套

✕ A: 把管辖限制硬扯成 equal protection，但本题先卡的是宪法管辖范围。

❌ 法律适用 | 例外授权误判

✕ C: 看到 exceptions and regulations 就以为国会能改原始管辖，错在把上诉管辖当成原始管辖。

❌ 事实误判 | 必要适当偷换

✕ D: 拿 necessary and proper 当万能钥匙，漏看它不能突破 Article III。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是终局上诉，再看是否落入 SCOTUS 的两类原始管辖，最后直接排除国会扩权说。

考场速记

记住一句：SCOTUS 原始管辖只有两扇门，大使/公使/领事 和 州是当事人；门外的案子，国会不能硬推进去。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，但那是中间上诉例外的记忆法，不是改写原始管辖的许可证。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law provides for an award of damages against anyone who publishes the name of a rape victim. Pursuant to that law, a woman sued a local newspaper in state court after the newspaper identified her as a rape victim.
The state trial and appellate courts rejected the claim, holding that the state law was invalid under both the state constitution and the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution. The state supreme court affirmed, holding specifically: "We think that this well-intentioned law very likely violates the First Amendment of the federal Constitution. We need not, however, decide that issue, because the law assuredly violates our state constitution, which provides even greater protection to the right of the press to report the news."
The woman petitioned for review in the U.S. Supreme Court.
Is the U.S. Supreme Court likely to review the state supreme court judgment?

choices.A: No, because the First Amendment prohibits the imposition of liability for the publication of truthful information.
choices.B: No, because the judgment of the state supreme court rests upon an adequate and independent state-law ground.
choices.C: Yes, because the supremacy clause does not permit a state to create rights greater than those conferred by the federal Constitution.
choices.D: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction extends to cases arising under federal law.

questions.explanation:
Adequate & independent state ground
(precludes SCOTUS review)
Adequate State ground fully resolves matter & application of federal law would not affect outcome
Independent State court did not rely on federal law to reach conclusion
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) may exercise its appellate jurisdiction to review a judgment of the highest court of a state if that judgment turned on federal law. But SCOTUS may not review a state court judgment that rests on an adequate and independent state ground—ie:

  • a state ground that fully resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case (adequate) and
  • the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its conclusion (independent).

Here, the state supreme court indicated that the state law very likely violates the U.S. Constitution. But the court also stated that it need not decide that federal issue because the law assuredly violates the state constitution. Since the state ground fully resolves the matter and the court did not rely on federal law to interpret the state constitution, SCOTUS is unlikely to review the state court judgment (Choice D).

(Choice A) The First Amendment freedom of the press generally bars liability for publicizing truthful information. But this does not provide a basis for SCOTUS to decline to review a case. Instead, review is improper here because the state court decision was based on an adequate and independent state ground.

(Choice C) The Article VI supremacy clause establishes that the U.S. Constitution and federal laws trump conflicting state laws. Therefore, states cannot restrict rights conferred by the U.S. Constitution. However, states are always free to create greater rights and protections than the U.S. Constitution does.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court cannot review a state court judgment that rests on an adequate and independent state ground—ie, (1) a state ground fully resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and (2) the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its conclusion.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (holding that a state supreme court can plainly state that its decision rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds).
  • 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 42 (2019) (explaining the adequate and independent state ground doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
一部州法律规定，对任何公布强奸案受害人姓名的人判处损害赔偿金。依据该法律，一名女性在当地一家报社指认其为强奸案受害人后，在州法院对该报社提起诉讼。

州初审法院和上诉法院驳回了该主张，认为该州法律根据州宪法和美国宪法第一修正案均属无效。州最高法院维持原判，并明确指出：“我们认为，这部用心良善的法律很可能违反了联邦宪法的第一修正案。然而，我们无需就此问题作出裁决，因为该法律确凿无疑地违反了我们的州宪法，而州宪法为新闻界报道新闻的权利提供了更强的保护。”

该女性请求美国最高法院进行复审。

美国最高法院是否可能复审州最高法院的判决？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为第一修正案禁止对发布真实信息的行为施加责任。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为州最高法院的判决依据的是充分且独立的州法律基础。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为至上条款不允许州创设比联邦宪法授予的权利更广泛的权利。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为美国最高法院的上诉管辖权延及根据联邦法律产生的案件。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review - Judicial Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州最高法院虽然提到联邦宪法，但它的判决已经稳稳建立在充分且独立的州法依据（adequate and independent state ground）上，所以 SCOTUS 不能接手改结果。

三秒认题路径：

州最高法院判了什么 → 只靠州法吗 → 联邦法会改结果吗 → 不能改 → 不受理

核心法律规则

美国最高法院（U.S. Supreme Court / SCOTUS）一般可以审查州最高法院的联邦法问题，但如果州法院判决建立在充分且独立的州法依据（adequate and independent state ground）上，SCOTUS 就不能复审。

充分（adequate）的意思是：州法本身就把案子完全解决了，就算不碰联邦法，结果也一样；独立（independent）的意思是：州法院没有靠联邦法来推出结论。

所以考试上只要看到“州法院说 we need not decide 联邦问题，因为州宪法已经够用了”，你就要立刻想到：SCOTUS 通常不能审。

核心判例： Michigan v. Long — 州最高法院如果明确表示自己是在充分且独立的州法依据上作出决定，联邦最高法院通常不进入实质审查。

思维导图

先问：这是州最高法院判决，SCOTUS 想不想审？
1. 是不是 终局判决（final judgment） 的州上诉结果？
YES 进入下一关：有没有州法挡路？
NO 这题不是终局性问题，直接看州法依据。
2. 州法院是不是说：联邦问题“不必决定”，因为州宪法已经足够解决？
YES 说明州法可以单独撑住结果。
NO 可能还有联邦审查空间。
3. 州法结论会不会被联邦法改掉结果？
卡死点：不能改结果 → adequate
州法院没靠联邦法推结论 → independent
结论：两关都过不了时，SCOTUS 不复审，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州法院都提到了 First Amendment，那 SCOTUS 应该能审。

但考试真正问的是：联邦问题有没有真的决定结果，还是州宪法已经单独把案子做完了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 州最高法院明确说“无需决定联邦问题”，而是靠州宪法就把案子判完了，所以属于 充分且独立的州法依据（adequate and independent state ground）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 这在偷换成第一修正案实体对错，不是在问 truthful information 能不能免审。

❌ 法律适用 | 联邦优先误判

✕ C: 这里不是在争州法能不能比联邦法给得更多，而是在看 supremacy clause 之外有没有州法独立挡门。

❌ 事实误判 | 终局路径偷换

✕ D: 只说 appellate jurisdiction 太笼统，忽略了州法已足以决定结果这一道门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看州法院有没有“州法单独结案”的表述，再判断联邦问题是不是只是陪跑。

考场速记

记住一句：州法已经把结果锁死，SCOTUS 就不进场；联邦法只有在真的会改结果时才有复审空间。

这类题就盯住 adequate 和 independent 两个词：一个管“结论能不能单独成立”，一个管“法院有没有靠联邦法”。
